precons.deckDescription: Uses negative Auras on opponents' creatures to weaken or neutralize them, while the goad mechanic forces opponents to attack each other. A political and disruptive deck that irritates opponents rather than winning through traditional combat or combos.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Goad mechanic; Auras on opponents' creatures; enchantress elements present but not central
precons.mainStrategy: Attach negative Auras to opponents' creatures to neutralize threats, then goad them into attacking each other, protecting yourself while others fight

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy disrupting opponents, political gameplay, and enchantment-based control rather than straightforward combat or combo wins
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer direct, aggressive strategies or dislike making enemies at the table
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for White/Black (Orzhov) players who value structure and ambition - using White's order/protection and Black's willingness to impose costs on others

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White brings structure and protection, while Black brings the willingness to weaken and exploit opponents. Together they create a deck that enforces rules on the table while making others pay for breaking them.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how White and Black combine control of social dynamics - White through rules-enforcement (goad) and Black through resource denial (negative Auras).
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not ideal for beginners due to the nuance of political gameplay, but great for players who have a basic grasp of Commander and want to explore social mechanics.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players that winning doesn't always require direct attacks - disrupting opponents and redirecting threats is a valid path to victory.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for teaching Goad and enchantment-based disruption; good case study for White-Black political identity.

precons.deckDescription: Focused on casting powerful and expensive instants and sorceries, with Elementals as a mascot creature type. Players who enjoy casting high-impact spells in a Izzet shell will find this deck satisfying.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Expensive instants and sorceries; Elemental creature type support; original Strixhaven Magma Opus referenced as flavor example
precons.mainStrategy: Cast large, impactful instants and sorceries for payoffs, supported by Elemental creature synergies

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love casting big spells and want a flashy, high-power spell-focused experience with a creature type subtheme
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer creature-heavy strategies or value-oriented board presence over spell-casting payoffs
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for Blue/Red (Izzet) personalities - Blue's love of knowledge and planning combined with Red's impulse and big dramatic plays

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue provides the calculation and card advantage needed to set up big spells, while Red provides the explosive, high-cost payoffs that make those spells devastating.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Izzet combines Blue's planning with Red's love of powerful, dramatic moments - using expensive spells as both the plan and the payoff.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Suited to players with some Commander experience who already understand resource management; introduces the spellslinger archetype.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches mana curve management and how to set up large spell turns by building resources over multiple turns.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example deck for explaining the spellslinger archetype and Blue-Red color identity.

precons.deckDescription: Combines sacrifice and life drain strategies with a new twist. Not the most original in concept, but strong for players who enjoy either or both themes. Offers fresh synergies between the two.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Sacrifice synergies; life drain effects; described as combining two fan-favorite themes
precons.mainStrategy: Sacrifice creatures and permanents to generate life drain effects, slowly bleeding opponents while extracting value from the graveyard

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy sacrifice-based aristocrat strategies and draining opponents' life totals for value
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike managing life totals or prefer combat-heavy or combo-focused strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Good fit for Black/Green (Golgari) players drawn to Black's resource-exchange and sacrifice themes combined with Green's creature base as fodder

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black brings the willingness to sacrifice and exploit, while Green provides the creature base and growth needed to fuel that sacrifice engine.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Black uses creatures as a resource rather than an end goal - with Green ensuring there is always more to sacrifice.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Good introduction to aristocrat-style play for players who understand basic creature combat and want to explore sacrifice synergies.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how sacrifice loops and life drain generate incremental advantage over a long game.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining Black-Green color identity and the classic aristocrats archetype on a basics page.

precons.deckDescription: The official Secrets of Strixhaven Lorehold deck led by Quintorius, History Chaser. Its commander turns cards leaving your graveyard into Spirit tokens, creating a specific graveyard-leaves and Spirit route.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Cards leaving graveyard synergies; Spirit creature type; commander is a planeswalker
precons.mainStrategy: Trigger effects by removing cards from the graveyard, supported by Spirit creature synergies, with the commander generating value from graveyard interaction

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy unusual graveyard-light strategies and tribal Spirit gameplay in an unexpected color combination
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players expecting a standard aggressive Red-White deck or those who dislike graveyard-dependent strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits White/Red players who appreciate order (White's structure) and passion (Red's emotion), channeled through a historically-flavored Spirit theme

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White brings structure and history-preservation while Red brings passion and the excitement of reclaiming what's been lost. Together they honor the past in a literal mechanical sense.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates that White-Red can do much more than aggro - it can build value engines around unusual synergies like graveyard departures.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not ideal for first-time players due to its unusual theme, but good for intermediate players who want to learn about graveyard triggers in a lower-power context.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to think about graveyard interaction in a non-traditional way - not filling it, but triggering effects when cards leave it.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of a White-Red deck that defies typical color expectations; useful for teaching color flexibility.

precons.deckDescription: A Blue-Green deck that uses +1/+1 counters as a subtheme, with X-cost spells as the primary focus. These flexible spells allow small early plays and explosively powerful late-game turns. The commander creates board states unlike other precons.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: +1/+1 counters; X-cost spells described as primary theme; flexible mana sinks; powerful late-game plays
precons.mainStrategy: Ramp into large X-cost spells for flexible, scalable effects, while using +1/+1 counters as a subtheme to support board presence

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy mathematical, flexible gameplay with powerful late-game turns and scalable spells
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer straightforward creature-based strategies or dislike managing multiple resource types
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Excellent fit for Blue/Green (Simic) players who value knowledge and planning (Blue) combined with growth and inevitability (Green)

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's analytical approach and Green's ramp capability combine to make X-cost spells scale in ways neither color could manage alone.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Blue's love of flexibility and optimization, plus Green's ramp as an engine that makes Blue's plans more powerful.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Best for players comfortable with mana management; teaches how X-cost spells scale with available mana.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about mana sinks and how to set up large turns with ramp and card advantage.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining Simic identity and how ramp plus card advantage creates powerful late-game turns.

precons.deckDescription: A five-color deck built around the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles IP. Offers significant customization via five partner commander options, allowing players to choose their preferred play style.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Partner commanders (five options); +1/+1 counters; Turtle creature type; commander selection as a feature
precons.mainStrategy: Select a commander from five partner options to customize play style, then build around Turtle tribal synergies and +1/+1 counter payoffs

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy flexibility and customization, TMNT fans, and players interested in five-color decks with tribal themes
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer focused, single-theme decks or those who dislike IP crossover sets
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits players who test across multiple color identities; the partner system mirrors a personality that values choice and adaptability over specialization

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: All five colors together represent a team of diverse skills working toward a common goal - a direct reflection of the TMNT's cooperative spirit.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Good introduction to five-color identity and how each color contributes a different role in a unified strategy.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: The partner system adds complexity, but the tribal focus makes it approachable for players familiar with creature-based strategies.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about Commander selection as a strategic choice and how different commanders dramatically change a deck's play pattern.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for introducing the partner mechanic and five-color identity on a basics page; also appeals to pop culture crossover players.

precons.deckDescription: A powerful five-color deck centered on casting massive Elementals using evoke costs granted by the commander, then sacrificing and copying them. Described as not a generic five-color goodstuff pile - it has a distinct, cohesive identity.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Evoke mechanic; sacrifice synergies; copying/duplicating creatures; Elemental creature type
precons.mainStrategy: Cast large Elementals cheaply via evoke, then sacrifice and copy them for massive value and board impact

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love casting giant creatures, exploring sacrifice and copy synergies, and playing unique five-color decks with a clear identity
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer straightforward aggro or linear strategies, or those who dislike complex board states
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits adventurous five-color players who value both power and creativity; aligns with Red's chaos and Green's love of massive creatures

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: All five colors are unified through elemental forces - each color's elemental creatures contributing to a singular powerful identity that transcends individual color philosophies.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows that five-color decks don't have to be unfocused - a strong tribal theme can give all five colors a unified purpose.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Complex for beginners due to evoke timing and sacrifice/copy interactions, but rewarding for players ready to learn stack mechanics.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about evoke as a value tool and how sacrifice and copy effects can generate disproportionate value from a single card.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for explaining the Evoke mechanic and how tribal synergies can unify a five-color identity.

precons.deckDescription: A Jund deck heavily featuring -1/-1 counters, a rare and unusual mechanic. Rewards applying counters to both your own and opponents' creatures. Despite the narrow theme, the deck offers meaningful upgrade directions and is described as powerful.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: -1/-1 counters on own and opponents' creatures; creature combos
precons.mainStrategy: Apply -1/-1 counters strategically to trigger rewards whether placed on your own or opponents' creatures, building toward creature-based combo payoffs

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy unusual, rarely-seen mechanics and are looking for a powerful, unique Jund deck with combo potential
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Beginners or players who prefer familiar, straightforward archetypes - this deck requires understanding of an unusual mechanic
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits Black/Red/Green (Jund) players who value power and are drawn to Black's willingness to harm their own resources and Red's chaotic energy

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black's willingness to harm and sacrifice, Red's aggression, and Green's creature base combine to weaponize weakness itself - turning -1/-1 counters into a strength.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Jund can turn debuffs into advantages, subverting the typical expectation that -1/-1 counters are purely negative.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not recommended for new players; best for experienced players familiar with counter mechanics who want something deeply unusual.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about symmetrical effects and how to build decks that benefit more from shared negative effects than opponents do.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for explaining rare mechanics and how color identity can subvert player expectations.

precons.deckDescription: A land sacrifice deck that generates benefits from sacrificing lands, with built-in recursion to return them from the graveyard. Enables powerful combos out of the box and scales easily with upgrades. The commander is a Spacecraft, reflecting new Edge of Eternities rules allowing legendary vehicles/spacecraft as commanders.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Sacrificing lands; land recursion from graveyard; combo-enabled; Spacecraft commander type
precons.mainStrategy: Sacrifice lands for powerful effects, then recur them from the graveyard to repeat the process, building toward land-based combo wins

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy land-based strategies, sacrifice loops, and combo-oriented gameplay with a unique mechanical identity
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer conventional creature or spell-based strategies, or beginners unfamiliar with land destruction effects
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits Green/Black/Red players who value Green's land-as-resource philosophy combined with Black's willingness to sacrifice and Red's explosive payoffs

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green's deep connection to lands meets Black's willingness to consume resources and Red's explosive destruction - lands become both fuel and engine.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Jund colors can approach land themes differently from typical Gruul land decks - treating lands as expendable combo pieces rather than stable mana bases.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Too complex for beginners; better suited to experienced players ready to explore land-based combo strategies.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about land sacrifice loops, graveyard recursion, and how to build self-sustaining resource engines.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining land sacrifice strategies and how Green's land philosophy can extend into sacrifice loops.

precons.deckDescription: An atypical artifact deck where artifacts serve as a subtheme to the main focus: proliferate with charge counters. Charge counters tied to artifacts are the key resource. The proliferate mechanic adds counters to any permanent or player already with counters. The commander is a Spacecraft reflecting new Edge of Eternities rules.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Proliferate; charge counters; artifacts; Mirrodin block flavor referenced; Spacecraft commander type
precons.mainStrategy: Use proliferate to stack charge counters on artifacts and other permanents, building incremental advantages and leveraging charge counter payoffs

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy counter-stacking strategies, artifact synergies, and the satisfaction of incremental advantage building through proliferate
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer aggressive or straightforward creature combat; those who dislike tracking multiple counter types
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits White/Blue/Red (Jeskai) players who value Blue's planning and methodical advantage with Red's artifact-invention energy and White's structural support

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's love of counters and incremental planning pairs with White's order and Red's inventive artifact affinity to build a methodical advantage engine.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Jeskai colors use artifacts and proliferate as tools of control and incremental value generation.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Moderately complex; best for players who understand basic artifact gameplay and want to explore counter manipulation.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about proliferate as a force multiplier and how charge counters create exponential value from artifacts.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent for explaining proliferate and charge counters; good example of how artifacts can serve as a secondary theme in a counter-focused deck.

precons.deckDescription: A Mardu reanimator deck based on Final Fantasy VI. Self-mills and discards to fill the graveyard, then recurs creatures using reanimation effects. A twist: the commander only reanimates creatures with 3 or less power, making it feel distinct from other reanimator piles.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Self-mill; discard effects; reanimation; commander restriction on 3 or less power creatures; Reanimate card included
precons.mainStrategy: Fill graveyard via self-mill and discard, then reanimate creatures - particularly those with 3 or less power per the commander's ability - to recur value efficiently

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Final Fantasy VI fans and players who enjoy graveyard-based reanimator strategies with a twist on creature power restrictions
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike graveyard-heavy strategies or those bothered by the self-mill vulnerability to exile effects
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits Black-primary players who value recursion and power through resource exchange, with White's protective elements and Red's impulse providing support

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black's dominion over death and recursion drives the engine, while White adds protective elements and Red provides discard and impulse draw to fuel the graveyard.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Illustrates how Mardu colors approach reanimation differently - using Black's death-recursion with Red's discard synergies as a unique filling mechanism.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Good introduction to reanimator strategy; the power restriction creates a teachable constraint that helps players understand how commander abilities shape deck construction.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches graveyard filling strategies and how creature power restrictions can create interesting deckbuilding constraints and decisions.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining the reanimator archetype and how self-mill and discard work as enablers rather than liabilities.

precons.deckDescription: A Naya Equipment deck themed around Final Fantasy VII and Cloud's Buster Sword. Provides a wide variety of equipment and bonus rewards for buffing the commander to 7 or more power. Strong pickup for equipment lovers and FF VII fans.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Equipment synergies; 7+ power threshold rewards; wide weapon variety
precons.mainStrategy: Equip Cloud and other creatures with a variety of weapons, trigger rewards at 7+ power, and win through combat with buffed creatures

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy equipment-focused voltron or go-wide combat strategies, FF VII fans, and those who want a relatively approachable aggressive deck
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer non-combat win conditions or dislike artifact-dependent strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for White/Red/Green (Naya) players who value Green's creature base, Red's aggression, and White's protective equipment synergies

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's protective order, Red's combat passion, and Green's creature power combine to make an offensive force equipped with legendary weapons.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Naya colors approach combat - not just through creatures, but through equipping them with tools that multiply their effectiveness.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: One of the more approachable FF precons; teaches equipment basics and combat threshold triggers in an intuitive way.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build toward a power threshold and how equipment synergies create combat advantages over multiple turns.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining Equipment and voltron-adjacent strategies; accessible to beginners learning about combat-focused precons.

precons.deckDescription: A Bant deck from Final Fantasy X centered on moving and manipulating counters on permanents. The main focus is +1/+1 counters, with a few other counter types in the mix. Proliferate is part of the strategy, making dice management essential.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Moving counters; +1/+1 counters; proliferate; multiple counter types; dice required
precons.mainStrategy: Manipulate and move counters around permanents, proliferate to stack them, and use counter-payoffs for value and board advantage

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy counter manipulation and proliferate strategies, especially FF X fans
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike tracking multiple counter types or prefer faster, more aggressive strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits White/Blue/Green (Bant) players - Blue's love of incremental advantage, Green's creature base, and White's supportive structure create a well-rounded counter engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's analytical precision, Green's growth, and White's protection combine to carefully grow and redistribute counters as a flexible resource.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Bant's strengths in incremental value and counter synergies - not as aggressive as Naya, but steadily building overwhelming board presence.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Moderate learning curve; teaches players about counter manipulation and the proliferate mechanic in an organized and manageable way.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how moving counters between permanents creates flexibility and how proliferate multiplies that advantage over time.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Solid example for explaining proliferate and counter-moving mechanics in a Bant shell.

precons.deckDescription: An Esper control deck based on Final Fantasy XIV. Less mechanically specific than the other FF precons - plays a general control game by removing threats, drawing cards, protecting itself, and slowly accruing value. Best for players who want to dictate game pace.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Card advantage; removal; protection; value generation; control-oriented
precons.mainStrategy: Control the game through removal and protection, draw cards consistently, and win through accumulated value advantage rather than a single explosive strategy

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy controlling the pace of games, drawing cards, and winning through incremental advantage rather than explosive turns
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer aggressive or combo-oriented strategies; those who dislike slow-building games
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Ideal for Blue-primary Esper players who value knowledge, planning, and control - with Black adding removal depth and White providing protective stability

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's control and card advantage, Black's removal depth, and White's protective structure make this deck a fortress of incremental value.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates the Esper control identity - not winning through a specific mechanism, but by outlasting and out-resourcing opponents.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not ideal for beginners due to reactive playstyle, but an excellent choice for players learning how to control the pace of Commander games.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about reactive decision-making, card advantage prioritization, and how control wins without a single dominant game plan.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining control archetypes and Esper color identity on a basics page.

precons.deckDescription: An unusual Abzan deck focused on high-toughness creatures and defenders. Normally defenders cannot attack, but the commander enables them to do so. Compared to the Doran, the Siege Tower archetype. Described as unusual but fun.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Defenders; high toughness; commander enables defenders to attack; Doran archetype comparison
precons.mainStrategy: Build a board of high-toughness defenders, use the commander to enable them to attack, and win through combat with creatures that opponents underestimate

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy subverting expectations, toughness-matters gameplay, and the novelty of attacking with defenders
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike aggressive combat strategies or prefer combo and control approaches
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Good fit for White/Black/Green (Abzan) players drawn to White's structure and endurance, Green's natural toughness, and Black's willingness to flip conventions

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's defensive protection, Green's natural toughness, and Black's subversive power combine to make defense into offense - a wall that fights back.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Abzan can take seemingly defensive resources and turn them into attacking threats, reflecting the color identities' combined resilience.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Accessible concept for new players; the theme of 'defenders that attack' is intuitive and easy to understand.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how to leverage overlooked stat lines (toughness) and how a single commander ability can flip a deck's entire gameplay.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining toughness-matters archetypes and how commanders can define unusual deckbuilding directions.

precons.deckDescription: A Mardu aggro deck with meaningful depth - not just straightforward beatdown. Combines aggressive token production with sacrifice synergies for a multi-layered, never-boring play experience.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Token production; sacrifice synergies; aggressive combat; multiple directions described
precons.mainStrategy: Create tokens quickly and attack aggressively, while using sacrifice synergies to generate additional value from those tokens and threaten opponents from multiple angles

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy aggressive token strategies with sacrifice depth; good for players who want more from aggro than just attacking
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer slower, more defensive or control-oriented strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for White/Black/Red (Mardu) players - White's tokens, Red's aggression, and Black's sacrifice combine for a multidimensional offensive identity

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Red's aggression drives the attack, White creates the token army, and Black ensures nothing dies without generating value - a relentless three-pronged offensive.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Mardu combines three aggressive colors into a deck that is more than the sum of its parts - aggression plus sacrifice creates a value loop.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Accessible for intermediate players; teaches how tokens and sacrifice work together in an intuitive way.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to balance aggression with sacrifice value - when to attack and when to sacrifice for maximum benefit.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining token-sacrifice synergies and Mardu color identity.

precons.deckDescription: A Jeskai spell-focused deck that rewards casting multiple spells of any card type. The top payoff is copying spells with the commander, enabling massively powerful turns. Described as containing fun combos and one of the more powerful Tarkir precon turns.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Prowess; casting multiple spells; spell copying with commander; noncreature spell focus with broader card type extension
precons.mainStrategy: Cast multiple spells in a turn to trigger prowess and other payoffs, then copy key spells with the commander for explosive value turns

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love chaining spells, creating explosive turns, and copy-spell combos in a Jeskai shell
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer creature-heavy or board-focused strategies; those who dislike managing stack complexity
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Excellent fit for White/Blue/Red (Jeskai) players - Blue's precision planning, Red's chaotic spell-slinging, and White's structural support enable perfectly timed explosive turns

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue plans the sequence, Red generates the impulsive power, and White holds the line - together making each turn a precisely orchestrated explosion.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Jeskai's identity as a spellcasting-focused color combination where casting multiple spells rewards careful sequencing.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Complex due to spell timing and copy interactions; better for intermediate players who want to learn advanced spell sequencing.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how to sequence spells for maximum impact and how copy effects create exponential value from a single card.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Great example for explaining prowess, spell copying, and how to build toward explosive turns in a spell-focused deck.

precons.deckDescription: A Temur Dragon ramp deck where the plan is to ramp into massive dragons. The secondary commander, Ureni of the Unwritten, is popular as an alternative commander for drawing and casting Dragons for free. Described as cool and deeply enjoyable for dragon and ramp lovers.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Ramp; Dragon tribal; casting Dragons for free with Ureni; secondary commander explicitly named
precons.mainStrategy: Ramp aggressively into the mid-to-late game, then cast massive Dragons for free or at a discount using the secondary commander, winning through dragon-powered combat

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Dragon enthusiasts, ramp lovers, and players who want a clear and satisfying game plan of building up to enormous creatures
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer combo or control strategies; those who want a more interactive or unique play pattern
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for Blue/Red/Green (Temur) players - Green's ramp, Red's dragon-fueled aggression, and Blue's card draw combine for an epic creature-casting experience

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green fuels the engine with ramp, Red brings the heart of dragons and fire, and Blue provides the card draw to find them - a triumvirate of power and inevitability.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Temur's identity as the color combination that produces the most explosive creature-based ramp strategies.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Accessible to beginners who want a simple game plan - ramp, then cast dragons. The straightforward strategy makes it good for newer players.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how ramp investment in early turns translates directly into late-game dominance through large creatures.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent beginner-accessible example for explaining Dragon tribal and ramp archetypes.

precons.deckDescription: A Sultai graveyard value deck. The theme is acknowledged as not the most original - it's straightforward graveyard value extraction. The 'Zombie Druid' branding on the box is noted as misleading, as there are no meaningful synergies with those types; they refer only to tokens generated by Teval, the Balanced Scale.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Graveyard value; tokens from Teval, the Balanced Scale mentioned; Zombie Druid noted as non-synergistic box text
precons.mainStrategy: Fill and exploit the graveyard for value, recurring resources and generating advantage through graveyard interaction in the classic Sultai style

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy graveyard-based value strategies and classic Sultai goodstuff gameplay
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players looking for unique or unusual mechanics; those who want something beyond the classic graveyard theme
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Solid fit for Blue/Black/Green (Sultai) players who value Black's graveyard dominion, Blue's card advantage, and Green's creature base as a graveyard engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black commands the graveyard, Blue selects what to fill and recur, and Green provides the creature density to make the engine run - classic Sultai value.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Sultai's three colors combine to make graveyard strategies reliable and consistent.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Good entry point for learning graveyard strategies in a controlled, manageable context; not as explosive as dedicated combo graveyard decks.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches core graveyard value principles - filling the graveyard intentionally and extracting incremental advantage from it.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Classic example for explaining Sultai identity and graveyard archetypes on a basics page.

precons.deckDescription: A Zombie deck with a twist - rather than spawning 2/2 tokens and relying heavily on traditional graveyard synergies, it pairs Zombie tribal with looting (drawing and discarding for card selection). The combination opens new possibilities beyond typical Zombie strategies.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Zombie tribal; looting (draw and discard); card selection; distinguished from traditional Zombie token strategies
precons.mainStrategy: Build a Zombie-based board while using looting to selectively fill the graveyard and find key pieces, combining tribal synergies with card selection advantage

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Zombie tribal fans who want a fresh take on the archetype and players who enjoy card selection through looting

precons.mainStrategy: Use Dogmeat to convert Junk tokens into Equipment and Auras, equip and enchant creatures for combat advantage, and press Naya's aggressive board presence

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Fallout fans, equipment lovers, and players who want a flavorful Naya deck that converts tokens into meaningful resources
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike relying on the commander's ability or those who find equipment-heavy strategies slow or dependent on specific pieces
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Good fit for White/Red/Green (Naya) players - White's ordered equipment structure, Red's aggressive deployment, and Green's creature base as equip targets

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White orders the equipment for maximum utility, Red drives the aggressive application, and Green provides the loyal creatures to carry those tools - Naya's warrior ethos made literal.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Naya combines its colors into a coherent combat-focused identity using both auras and equipment in a single unified strategy.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Equipment and Aura basics are taught in an approachable context; the Junk token conversion adds a creative twist that makes the strategy feel special.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to leverage token resources for card advantage and how Auras and Equipment complement each other in a combat strategy.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for Naya Aura/Equipment identity and introducing the concept of converting tokens into meaningful permanents.

precons.deckDescription: A Jeskai energy deck that also features an artifact secondary theme. Among the first to revive the long-forgotten energy mechanic from Kaladesh. Combines iconic characters and locations from the Fallout universe with thematically fitting energy and artifact gameplay.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Energy counters; artifacts; Kaladesh mechanic revival; Fallout-flavored characters and locations
precons.mainStrategy: Generate and spend energy counters for powerful effects, with artifact synergies supporting the engine and Fallout-themed cards providing flavorful payoffs

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Fallout fans, energy enthusiasts, and players who want a Jeskai artifact-energy deck with strong flavor integration
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer combat-heavy strategies or those who find managing energy as a secondary currency cumbersome
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Good fit for Jeskai (White/Blue/Red) players who value Blue's scientific methodology, Red's Kaladesh-style inventive energy, and White's structured artifact assembly

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's scientific precision manages the energy economy, Red's inventive spirit generates it, and White's structure assembles the artifact framework - a technological powerhouse.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Jeskai expresses a 'science and technology' identity through energy and artifacts, connecting thematic flavor to mechanical function.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Energy works best when learned through play; this deck gives a full energy experience in a thematically coherent Fallout context.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how energy and artifacts synergize as layered resource systems and how to evaluate the best uses of energy for maximum effect.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for introducing energy as a Kaladesh-era mechanic and showing how it functions in a Jeskai artifact context.

precons.deckDescription: A Mardu aristocrats deck led by Caesar from Fallout, who sacrifices anything for power. Sacrifice synergies and creature tokens are the core themes. Recommended for traditional aristocrat strategy fans even beyond Fallout interest.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Sacrifice synergies; creature tokens as sacrifice fodder; aristocrats archetype; Caesar flavor match
precons.mainStrategy: Generate creature tokens and use them as sacrifice fodder to trigger aristocrat-style payoffs, building advantage through the sacrifice loop and pressuring opponents with life loss and value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Aristocrat strategy lovers, Fallout fans, and players who enjoy managing a sacrifice engine with token generation
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer combat-focused or spell-heavy strategies without the complexity of sacrifice timing
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for White/Black/Red (Mardu) players - White provides the token army, Black drives the sacrifice engine, Red adds aggressive pressure from the sacrifice payoffs

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White creates the token army, Black converts their deaths into power, and Red channels that power into aggressive punishment - Caesar's empire built on sacrifice.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Mardu's aristocrat identity - White and tokens as fuel, Black as the sacrificial engine, and Red as the aggressive payoff channel.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: The aristocrats archetype requires some experience to play optimally; good for intermediate players learning how sacrifice timing creates advantage.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches classic aristocrat strategy: generate tokens, sacrifice them for value, and repeat - while managing when to sacrifice versus when to attack.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Classic aristocrats example in a Mardu shell; good for explaining sacrifice-based value engines on a basics page.

precons.deckDescription: The most unusual Fallout deck, featuring milling as a primary theme alongside the new rad counters mechanic. Rad counters are placed on players, causing them to mill and eventually take damage. Described as fascinating play patterns for players tired of conventional strategies.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Mill; rad counters placed on players; rad counters cause milling and damage; unusual mechanic combination
precons.mainStrategy: Place rad counters on opponents to force them to mill their own libraries and take incremental damage, while using the milling process to deplete opponents' resources and win through library attrition or damage

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love unique mechanics, mill strategies, and Fallout flavor; those who want something genuinely different from typical Commander archetypes
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike mill strategies or find non-combat win conditions unsatisfying; those who prefer combat-heavy gameplay
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Fits Blue/Black/Green (Sultai) players - Blue's knowledge-stripping mill, Black's attrition-through-damage, and Green's mana base enabling a unique resource-denial strategy

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue strips away knowledge (mill), Black converts that loss into damage through rad counters, and Green provides the mana base for sustained attrition - a creeping, unavoidable doom.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Sultai's ability to win through resource denial and attrition rather than direct combat, demonstrating the colors' combined capacity for patient destruction.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not suitable for beginners due to the unusual rad counter mechanic; best for players who want to learn a truly novel strategy.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how rad counters create a unique form of damage that bypasses life total directly, and how mill functions as both disruption and win condition.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for introducing rad counters and mill as alternate win conditions on a basics page.

precons.productSection: Murders at Karlov Manor Commander Precons
precons.deckDescription: Entirely built around forcing opponents to attack using the Goad mechanic and related effects. Rewards result from those forced attacks. Creates active, aggressive games - described as great for players bored by table stalling.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Goad; forcing opponents to attack; rewards for forced attacking; active game encouragement
precons.mainStrategy: Goad opponents' creatures to force combat actions, direct that violence between opponents, and collect rewards from the chaos of forced attacks while protecting yourself

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy active, combat-filled Commander games and want to force action at the table without being the primary aggressor
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer passive, value-building strategies or those who want consistent combos over table chaos
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for White/Red (Boros) players - White's ordered fairness in distributing attacks, Red's impulsive aggression, and the combined desire for an active, moving game

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White brings the command structure that orders who must fight, and Red provides the chaotic energy that turns the forced combat into an explosive free-for-all.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Boros's unique ability to control the combat step through forced engagement - using White's order and Red's aggression in a political-combat hybrid.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Relatively accessible - Goad is easy to understand conceptually - and great for players learning about political mechanics in Commander.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how Goad creates political dynamics, forces opponents to interact with each other, and protects the caster from becoming the target.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for explaining Goad and political combat mechanics; clean demonstration of Boros identity.

precons.productSection: Murders at Karlov Manor Commander Precons
precons.deckDescription: Combines Surveil (look at top cards, put them in graveyard or back on top) with reanimation. Surveil sets up the graveyard, then reanimation exploits it cheaply. Contains strong reanimator reprints, described as an excellent entry point for the archetype.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Surveil; reanimation; graveyard setup; strong reprints for reanimator strategy
precons.mainStrategy: Use Surveil to set up the graveyard with high-value targets, then reanimate them cheaply to generate overwhelming board states and value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players interested in learning the reanimator archetype; Blue-Black fans who want graveyard depth combined with library manipulation
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players in groups with heavy graveyard hate; those who prefer proactive board-presence strategies over reactive reanimation
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for Blue/Black (Dimir) players - Blue's top-deck manipulation enables Black's graveyard dominion in a clean, synergistic two-color pairing

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue curates the graveyard with precision through Surveil, while Black commands what lies within it - a perfectly synchronized information-and-recursion engine.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Blue's knowledge management and Black's graveyard power work together as a singular strategy.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Good entry point for reanimator - Surveil teaches players to consciously manage their graveyard as a resource rather than treating it as a discard pile.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches graveyard-as-resource philosophy and how Surveil creates intentional setup for reanimation rather than leaving it to chance.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent for explaining Surveil and reanimation on a basics page; clean two-color example of Dimir graveyard identity.

precons.productSection: Murders at Karlov Manor Commander Precons
precons.deckDescription: A face-down card deck in Naya colors - described as an unexpected combination. Uses Morph, Megamorph, Disguise, and Cloak to fill the board with hidden creatures that opponents cannot identify. Excellent for players who want to keep opponents guessing.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Morph; Megamorph; Disguise; Cloak; face-down creatures; synergies with face-down cards
precons.mainStrategy: Fill the board with face-down creatures using Morph, Megamorph, Disguise, and Cloak, then reveal them at optimal times to surprise opponents and leverage face-down synergies

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy keeping opponents guessing, hidden information gameplay, and mastering complex turn-flip timing with face-down mechanics
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer transparent board states or those who find tracking face-down cards at the table cumbersome
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Interesting fit for White/Red/Green (Naya) players who want to combine Naya's creature power with the deceptive elements more typical of Blue

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White structures the face-down formation, Red provides the impulsive reveal moments, and Green supplies the powerful creatures worth hiding - Naya's strength made secretive.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Naya can incorporate deception mechanics normally associated with other colors, showing the breadth of face-down card design space.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Face-down mechanics require understanding of turn-up costs and timing; better for intermediate players comfortable with creature combat.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players about hidden information as a strategic resource and how face-down cards create opponent decision paralysis.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for explaining the full suite of face-down mechanics (Morph, Megamorph, Disguise, Cloak) in one deck.

precons.productSection: Murders at Karlov Manor Commander Precons
precons.deckDescription: Centered around Clue tokens - artifacts sacrificed for card draw by paying two mana. Provides many ways to use Clues beyond simple card draw. Plays as expected from a Bant deck: abundant card draw, value, and decision points. Note: the source body text calls this deck 'Deep Blue Sea' but the canonical name from the product section header is 'Deep Clue Sea.'
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Clue tokens; artifact sacrifice for card draw; multiple Clue uses; Bant value and card draw; decision-rich gameplay
precons.mainStrategy: Generate and exploit Clue tokens for card draw and other uses, building overwhelming card advantage in a Bant shell and winning through resource dominance and decision-point saturation

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love card advantage, artifact tokens, and Bant-style value accumulation; those who enjoy decks with many decision points
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer aggressive or combat-heavy strategies; those who find incremental value-building too slow
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Strong fit for White/Blue/Green (Bant) players - White's structured Clue investigation, Blue's card draw mastery, and Green's mana support create an overwhelming value engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White structures the investigation framework, Blue turns every Clue into knowledge and card advantage, and Green provides the mana base to activate them - Bant's value-engine identity crystallized.
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Bant colors build overwhelming value engines through artifact tokens - combining White's structure, Blue's card draw, and Green's mana into a unified advantage machine.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Clue tokens are intuitive - pay two mana, draw a card - making this approachable for players learning about artifact tokens and card advantage.
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how artifact tokens can serve multiple purposes beyond their obvious function and how to build engines around repeatable token generation.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for introducing Clue tokens, Bant value strategies, and artifact-based card advantage on a basics page.

precons.deckDescription: A Morph-focused Commander deck built to cast face-down creatures efficiently and draw a card from the first one cast each turn. Kadena keeps opponents guessing while generating card advantage, then flips creatures at the right moment for surprise impact. A deception-based value engine that rewards patience and timing.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Morph; free morph cost with Kadena; card draw on morph cast; face-down hidden information; optimal flip timing
precons.mainStrategy: Cast creatures face-down for free, draw a card each time, flip at optimal moments to surprise opponents

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy hidden information, deception, and card-draw engines via face-down mechanics
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer transparent board states or straightforward aggro
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Sultai players drawn to knowledge-hiding and value accumulation over direct power

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's information control + Black's subversion + Green's creature base enable a deck where nothing is as it seems
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Sultai combines Blue's information control (hidden face-down cards) with Black's subversive deception and Green's creature density - each color contributing a different dimension to the morph engine.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Introduces Morph timing and how hidden information creates opponent decision paralysis
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to manage a dual resource: the face-down board creates threat ambiguity for opponents while Kadena's card draw keeps your hand full - both resources must be managed simultaneously for optimal play.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Ideal for explaining the Morph mechanic on a basics page; shows how hidden information creates strategic depth and teaches Sultai's identity as the color combination that weaponizes knowledge asymmetry.

precons.deckDescription: A Flashback-focused Jeskai deck that casts spells from the graveyard for repeated value. Sevinne's ability to copy the first instant or sorcery cast from the graveyard each turn creates explosive multi-spell turns. Contains strong iconic cards for the spellslinger and Flashback archetypes.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Flashback; graveyard spell casting; Sevinne copy trigger on first graveyard cast; instants and sorceries matter
precons.mainStrategy: Cast spells from the graveyard via Flashback, generating repeated value from the same cards

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Spellslinger players who want to re-use instants and sorceries from the graveyard
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players seeking a flashy or highly novel mechanic; primarily creature-focused players
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Jeskai players who value getting double value from every spell they cast

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Jeskai colors use Blue's knowledge, Red's impulsive spells, and White's structure to re-cast and re-use spells for maximum efficiency
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Jeskai combines Blue's recursive knowledge (re-casting spells) with Red's impulsive spell power and White's structural protection - the Flashback mechanic literalizes Blue's philosophy of learning from the past.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches graveyard-as-resource via Flashback - spells don't have to be one-time-use
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to treat the graveyard as a second hand - identifying which spells are most valuable to Flashback and sequencing Sevinne's copy trigger for maximum double-spell turns.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining Flashback on a basics page and demonstrating how Jeskai approaches the graveyard as a knowledge resource rather than a pure death zone.

precons.deckDescription: A Populate-focused Naya token deck that creates powerful creature tokens early, then copies the best one repeatedly in the mid and late game. Ghired enters creating a 4/4 Rhino, which becomes the primary Populate target for subsequent turns. A straightforward but effective go-wide token strategy.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Populate; token copying; Rhino token as primary populate target; go-wide combat
precons.mainStrategy: Make powerful tokens early (often 4/4 Rhinos), then Populate them in the mid/late game for overwhelming board presence

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Token and aggro players who want to make large tokens and copy them for a dominating board state
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Control or combo players; those who dislike combat-focused strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Naya players who want explosive token-based board development

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Naya's White tokens, Red aggression, and Green creature power combine to make Populate a devastating snowball mechanic
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Illustrates how Naya channels White's token army, Red's aggressive momentum, and Green's creature power into the Populate mechanic - copying your best token amplifies all three colors' strengths simultaneously.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Populate - copying your best token rather than making weak generic ones
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players that token quality beats token quantity - making one powerful token (like Ghired's 4/4 Rhino) and Populating it repeatedly is more efficient than flooding the board with 1/1s.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining the Populate mechanic on a basics page; shows how Naya's go-wide token identity can copy a chosen token repeatedly.

precons.deckDescription: A Madness-focused Rakdos deck built around Anje Falkenrath's ability to tap for draw-and-discard, enabling free or discounted Madness spells every turn. Scales easily toward competitive play through reanimation of discarded threats. Considered one of the highest-ceiling precons ever printed.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Madness; Anje Falkenrath tap ability; discard as resource; Madness cost reduction; reanimation of discarded creatures; near-cEDH potential
precons.mainStrategy: Discard cards constantly for Madness cost savings and Anje's ability triggers; reanimate discarded creatures; near-cEDH viable with minimal upgrades

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Competitive-leaning players who want a Madness/discard combo deck that scales easily toward cEDH
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Beginners or casual players who prefer fair, interactive gameplay
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Rakdos players drawn to maximum resource exploitation and high-speed combo potential

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black's willingness to spend resources and Red's impulsive discard combine to turn every discarded card into fuel
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Captures Rakdos at its most resource-efficient - Black's willingness to spend life and discard cards pairs with Red's impulsive discard-for-value to make every resource expenditure simultaneously a gain through Madness.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not for beginners - teaches advanced discard-as-resource and combo assembly
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches the advanced concept of discard-as-resource: building a deck where discarding is never a cost but always a trigger, and understanding how Anje's tap ability creates an infinite loop of draw-discard-cast.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent advanced example for a basics page on Madness and discard synergies; demonstrates how Rakdos can make losing resources feel like gaining them.

precons.deckDescription: A Saheeli-led Izzet artifact deck that reduces costs with each cheap artifact cast, then deploys one dominant artifact threat. The strategy rewards flooding the board with small artifacts early to make Saheeli's second ability affordable. Contains several strong new artifact-focused cards.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Artifact cost reduction via Saheeli; cheap artifacts as ramp enablers; big artifact threat as win condition
precons.primaryTheme: Artifacts / cheap artifact ramp into big artifact threats
precons.mainStrategy: Cast many cheap artifacts to trigger Saheeli's cost reduction, then ramp into a single massive artifact threat

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Artifact lovers who want an Izzet deck focused on ramping into one dominant artifact threat
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Creature-focused or combat-heavy players; those wanting a more interactive play pattern
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Izzet players interested in artifacts over spellslinging

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Izzet's inventive Red and precise Blue combine to build and deploy artifacts faster than any other color pair
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Izzet's inventor identity - Blue provides the precise engineering to play many cheap artifacts and Red supplies the inventive ambition to deploy one massive artifact payoff, with Saheeli's cost reduction bridging the two.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how cost reduction stacks with small artifacts to enable early access to expensive payoffs
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches ramp through artifact volume rather than land-based ramp - counting Saheeli's cost reduction triggers as a mana acceleration mechanic and planning the big artifact deployment turn from the first card played.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining cost reduction mechanics on a basics page; shows how Izzet builds mana acceleration through artifact density rather than traditional ramp spells.

precons.deckDescription: A Lord Windgrace-led Jund lands deck with landfall and land recursion as its primary engines. Windgrace's planeswalker abilities recur lands from the graveyard and generate card advantage directly through land interaction. Somewhat underdelivers on land synergies beyond the commander itself.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Landfall; land recursion from graveyard via Windgrace; land-based card draw; Windgrace planeswalker abilities
precons.mainStrategy: Leverage Lord Windgrace's land-focused abilities to recur and replay lands, generating value through landfall and land-based effects

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Land strategy enthusiasts in Jund colors who want landfall and land recursion in a single cohesive package
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players wanting a fully creature-centric or combat-heavy Jund deck; noted as underdelivering on land synergies beyond the commander
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Jund players interested in land-as-resource strategy rather than standard creature aggro

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Jund's Black sacrifice, Red destruction, and Green growth all apply to lands - treating the mana base itself as a renewable engine
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Jund treats lands as weapons - Black sacrifices them, Red destroys with them, and Green grows through them, with Lord Windgrace making the mana base itself the primary resource engine.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how lands can be a primary resource engine, not just mana sources
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players that lands can be a renewable sacrifice resource rather than permanent fixtures - Windgrace's recursion loop shows how the same land can enter and generate value multiple times per game.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for a basics page on lands-matter strategies; useful for explaining how Jund's three aggressive colors can approach land interaction from a value-engine rather than purely destructive perspective.

precons.deckDescription: An Estrid-led Bant enchantress deck that builds a card-draw engine by casting enchantments while generating mana through Estrid's untap ability. The classic enchantress loop - each enchantment draws a card, enabling the next - is the deck's core engine.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Enchantress draw triggers; Estrid untap ability as mana engine; Aura synergies; enchantments matter
precons.mainStrategy: Build an enchantress engine - play enchantments to draw cards, generate mana via Estrid's untap, and win through enchantment-based value accumulation

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Enchantment lovers who want a cohesive Bant enchantress deck with ramp and card draw built in
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer creature-combat or artifact-based strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Bant players aligned with Blue-Green's growth-through-knowledge philosophy, extended into enchantment permanents

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Bant's White structure, Blue card draw, and Green ramp make enchantments both the engine and the payoff
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Showcases Bant's enchantment identity at its most cohesive - White structures the enchantment framework, Blue draws cards from each enchantment cast, and Green generates the mana through Estrid's untap, making all three colors essential to the engine.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Classic enchantress lesson: each enchantment you cast replaces itself and enables the next - a self-sustaining value loop
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches the classic enchantress loop: each enchantment replaces itself through card draw, enabling the next enchantment, which enables the next - the deck accelerates itself and the key skill is knowing which enchantments break the loop open.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful enchantress archetype example for explaining how White-Blue-Green approaches enchantments as both the engine and the payoff simultaneously.

precons.deckDescription: An Aminatou-led Esper deck combining top-of-library manipulation with the Miracle mechanic for cost-reduced spells and ETB blink value. The most complex C18 deck, rewarding players who can engineer their draw step to set up Miracle triggers and chain blink effects. Contains powerful reprints for all three strategies.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Miracle cost reduction; top-of-library manipulation; ETB blink via Aminatou minus ability; library order engineering
precons.mainStrategy: Manipulate the top card of the library to always draw the most useful card; use Miracle to cast those cards for reduced cost; blink permanents with Aminatou for ETB value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Advanced players who enjoy precision library control, Miracle triggers, and ETB blink value in a controlling Esper shell
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Beginners or players who prefer aggro/combat; extremely complex to pilot optimally
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Esper players who want maximum information control and deliberate play patterns

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Esper's Blue precision and Black depth combine with White's order to curate the future - every draw is a deliberate choice
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Esper's most cerebral identity - Blue engineers the library order with precision, White provides Miracle's protective cost reduction, and Black adds the recursive depth that makes the engine resilient to disruption.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not for beginners - teaches advanced library manipulation and how to engineer draw steps
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches top-deck engineering as an active skill: using Aminatou's +1 to set up Miracle triggers, her -1 to blink permanents for ETB chains, and sequencing both abilities to maximize value while maintaining library control every turn.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Advanced example for a basics page on library manipulation and Miracle, showing how Esper can win through information control rather than direct power.

precons.deckDescription: A five-color Dragon tribal deck led by The Ur-Dragon, whose eminence ability reduces Dragon casting costs by one from the command zone. It aims to flood the board with Dragons and win through aerial combat.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Eminence cost reduction; Dragon tribal; five-color mana base; combat overwhelm with flying Dragons
precons.mainStrategy: Use Ur-Dragon's eminence to reduce Dragon casting costs, flood the board with Dragons as fast as possible, and win through combat overwhelm

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Dragon fans and players who want a straightforward but powerful five-color tribal aggro deck
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer combo, control, or non-creature strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Five-color players who want a focused tribal identity rather than goodstuff

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: All five colors exist solely to enable the ultimate tribe - Dragons - whose power transcends any single color's philosophy
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows that five colors can have a singular focused identity - every color contributes its best Dragons and its mana base to one unified goal, teaching players that five-color doesn't mean unfocused.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Approachable for beginners - ramp into Dragons, attack. Teaches eminence as a passive command zone benefit
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how Eminence functions as a passive cost reduction that makes the entire tribe cheaper from turn one, and how to sequence Dragon deployment to maximize the passive benefit before ever casting Ur-Dragon.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining Eminence on a basics page; demonstrates five-color tribal identity and how a passive command-zone ability can define a deck's strategy.

precons.deckDescription: An Arahbo-led Selesnya Cat tribal deck that uses Arahbo's eminence to pump a Cat at the start of combat every turn. Equipment synergies provide additional power through Nazahn's ability to tutor and auto-equip. Straightforward but effective tribal aggro in Green-White.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Eminence combat pump; Cat tribal; equipment synergy via Nazahn; power boosting on attack
precons.mainStrategy: Build a board of Cats, boost their power with Arahbo's eminence, and win through combat with pumped feline creatures

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Cat tribal fans and players who want a clean, approachable Selesnya aggro deck with equipment synergies
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Control or combo players; those who find tribal strategies too linear
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Selesnya players who want tribal focus and straightforward combat aggression

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's order and protection combined with Green's creature power create a disciplined hunting pack that strikes hard and fast
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Illustrates how Selesnya approaches tribal combat - White provides the protective structure and pump that makes each Cat valuable, while Green supplies the creature density that makes Arahbo's eminence consistently relevant.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Very beginner-accessible: play Cats, pump them with Arahbo, attack - a clean and intuitive game plan
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how Eminence combat pump works differently from static anthems - it targets one Cat per turn, teaching players to identify which Cat benefits most from the free +3/+3 and trample in each specific combat situation.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Clean Selesnya tribal example for a basics page; useful for explaining how Eminence creates a passive benefit that rewards the commander never needing to be cast.

precons.deckDescription: An Edgar Markov-led Mardu Vampire tribal deck. Edgar's eminence ability creates a 1/1 Vampire token whenever a Vampire spell is cast, building a wide board without needing to cast Edgar himself and creating steady combat pressure.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Eminence token generation; Vampire tribal; token flooding on every Vampire cast; aggressive go-wide combat
precons.mainStrategy: Use Edgar's eminence to flood the board with Vampire tokens every time a Vampire is cast, creating an unstoppable wide army that overwhelms opponents unless they answer the board every single turn

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Vampire fans and aggressive token players who want command-zone token generation
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer slow, deliberate strategies; this deck demands opponents answer it every turn
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mardu players who want consistent, pressure-forward aggro that never lets opponents breathe

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Mardu's Red aggression, White token production, and Black's vampire ambition combine into the most relentless tribal aggro identity in Commander
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Mardu tribal at its most aggressive - White generates the token army, Red drives it into relentless combat, and Black adds the sacrifice and recursion depth that makes the Vampire swarm perpetually threatening.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Clean lesson in how eminence enables passive token generation - every spell cast becomes two threats
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches the power of command zone presence - Edgar never needs to be cast for his eminence to flood the board, teaching players to evaluate when casting the commander adds value versus keeping him as a passive engine.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining token-flooding tribal strategies and how a commander can affect the game from the command zone without being cast.

precons.deckDescription: An Inalla-led Grixis Wizard tribal deck that uses Inalla's eminence to create a copy of each Wizard on ETB for one mana, doubling every enter-the-battlefield trigger. The deck's power comes from chaining high-value Wizard ETBs and doubling them for overwhelming value. Features several powerful new Wizard cards.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Eminence ETB copying; Wizard tribal; ETB trigger doubling; creature-based control and value
precons.mainStrategy: Play Wizards with powerful ETB triggers; use Inalla's eminence to copy them and double the triggers for overwhelming value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy ETB value-stacking, creature-based control, and Grixis color identity with a tribal focus
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer combat aggro or simple token strategies; ETB stacking requires careful sequencing
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Grixis players who want tribal depth combined with complex ETB value chains

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Grixis's Blue intellect, Black cunning, and Red impulsiveness merge in the Wizard type - each ETB trigger a spell-like effect doubled by Inalla
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Grixis focuses its three colors through a single creature type - Blue's Wizard intellect, Black's cunning utility creatures, and Red's impulsive ETB payoffs all combine through Inalla's doubling to create a value chain greater than any individual part.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches ETB trigger stacking and how eminence copy effects create exponential value
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches ETB sequencing as a skill - identifying which Wizards have the best ETB abilities to double with Inalla, and how to chain those doubled triggers for maximum value in a single turn.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining ETB doubling and Eminence on a basics page; demonstrates how Grixis approaches tribal through ability chains rather than pure creature power.

precons.deckDescription: A Yidris-led four-color Cascade deck that gives all spells cast this turn Cascade after Yidris deals combat damage. Each Cascade hit can chain into further Cascades for explosive value turns. Contains several notable partner commanders and cards that became staples.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Cascade on all spells after combat damage; Undaunted mechanic; four-color without White; chain Cascade potential; partner commanders
precons.mainStrategy: Deal combat damage with Yidris to give all spells cast this turn Cascade, chaining into random but powerful free spells for chaotic value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love chaotic, unpredictable games and cascading into unexpected free spells
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want consistent, predictable game plans; Cascade outcomes are inherently random
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Four-color players who embrace chaos and spontaneity over control

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Four-color without White means no order - Blue's plans, Black's cunning, Red's chaos, and Green's power combine into an unstoppable cascade of randomness
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates four-color Cascade as the ultimate expression of Blue-Black-Red-Green's combined unpredictability - each Cascade hit could generate any spell in the deck, and the deck is built to make every random hit as valuable as possible.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not for beginners - teaches Cascade mechanics and how to build a deck that benefits from random free spells
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches Cascade deck construction: understanding how CMC distribution affects Cascade hits, how to build a curve where random hits are rarely wasted, and how Yidris's combat damage requirement creates a meaningful timing decision each turn.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining Cascade; teaches how the mechanic rewards careful deck construction and why mana-value management matters in chaos-themed decks.

precons.deckDescription: A Saskia-led, direct combat-focused four-color deck built around efficient creatures and Saskia's ability to deal damage to a second player. It aims to end games through combat-damage amplification.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Damage doubling to second player via Saskia; four-color without Blue; aggressive creature scaling; combat-focused win condition
