precons.mainStrategy: Play cheap creatures that grow, attack aggressively, and use Saskia's ability to double combat damage by targeting a second player - overwhelming the table quickly

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who want a direct, combat-focused four-color game plan
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Combo or control players; those who dislike being the table's primary threat
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Four-color aggro players who want to end games fast and directly

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Without Blue's hesitation, the remaining four colors push pure aggression - the warrior identity across White order, Black sacrifice, Red fire, and Green power
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows four-color aggro without Blue's hesitation - Black's sacrifice, Red's fire, Green's power, and White's martial discipline all push the same direction, teaching players that color combinations without one color can still achieve extreme synergy.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Simple and accessible concept: attack, hit two players at once with Saskia, end the game
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how Saskia's second-player damage trigger creates a political decision every attack - choosing which opponent to designate doubles all damage dealt, making each combat a strategic choice about who to pressure most.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Clean example for explaining combat damage amplification on a basics page; demonstrates how four-color decks can have a completely focused identity despite spanning multiple colors.

precons.deckDescription: A Kynaios and Tiro-led four-color group hug deck that gives all players extra cards, lands, and resources each turn while benefiting more from those gifts than opponents. The original group hug Commander precon, featuring the Join Forces mechanic and broad four-color access for political tools.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Group hug resource sharing; Join Forces mechanic; four-color without Black; benefit-more-than-opponents design; political alliances
precons.mainStrategy: Give opponents extra cards, lands, and resources while benefiting more yourself; use political alliances to survive and be the last player standing

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy group hug politics and want the original group-hug precon with broad color access
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer competitive or combat-focused gameplay; group hug is polarizing
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Four-color players with strong White/community personality alignment who want to win through politics

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: All colors except Black - without the will to dominate, the deck enables genuine generosity, using the table's goodwill as its defense
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Illustrates four colors without Black's selfishness - Red, Green, White, and Blue all have cooperative instincts that Kynaios and Tiro exploit, teaching players that color philosophy directly shapes which multiplayer strategies are possible.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches group hug and Join Forces as political tools - sharing to survive
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches that giving resources to opponents can be a winning strategy when you benefit more from those gifts than they do - and how Join Forces mechanics create political moments where cooperation is genuinely in everyone's interest.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Ideal for explaining group hug and Join Forces on a basics page; demonstrates how color philosophy (no Black) enables a cooperative strategy that would be impossible with a different color combination.

precons.deckDescription: An Atraxa-led four-color proliferate deck that adds counters across several permanent and player types. It supports +1/+1 counters, planeswalker loyalty, poison counters, and charge counters in the same shell.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Proliferate every upkeep; +1/+1 counters; planeswalker loyalty advancement; poison counter support; charge counters
precons.mainStrategy: Place +1/+1 counters on creatures and proliferate every turn with Atraxa, exponentially growing threats and any other counters on the board

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who want a counter-based commander that can support several proliferate strategies
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike tracking many counter types or those who find Atraxa a high-priority removal target in their playgroup
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Four-color players who value sustained growth over explosive moments; the defining proliferate commander

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Four colors without Red - deliberate, not impulsive - White's order, Blue's growth through knowledge, Black's ambition, and Green's proliferating nature
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Captures four colors without Red's impulsiveness - White's order, Blue's precision, Black's ambition, and Green's growth all serve Atraxa's patient proliferate engine, demonstrating how Atraxa's colors naturally support a scaling rather than explosive strategy.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches proliferate as a force multiplier - every counter doubles its impact each rotation
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches proliferate as a force multiplier: every counter on every permanent grows each upkeep, creating compound growth that makes early investment pay off exponentially - the key skill is placing the first counters correctly.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful proliferate archetype example showing how one mechanic can unify four colors into a coherent strategy.

precons.deckDescription: A Breya-led four-color artifact deck that uses Breya's sacrifice ability as a repeatable removal and life-drain tool. The deck supports artifact combo lines through the sacrifice loop and contains several artifact-focused partner commanders.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Artifact sacrifice for removal and life drain; Breya combo potential; four-color without Green; artifact token generation; partner commanders
precons.mainStrategy: Build an artifact board, use Breya's sacrifice ability as a repeatable removal and life-drain tool, and win through artifact-based combo or value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Artifact combo players who want a four-color shell with flexible sacrifice-based removal and loop potential
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer creature-based or land-based strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Four-color players drawn to artifact combo and the most artifact-synergistic color combination possible

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: All colors except Green (which dislikes artifacts) - this is the definitive artifact identity across White, Blue, Black, and Red
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates four colors without Green's dislike of artifacts - White, Blue, Black, and Red each contribute a different relationship with artifice to make Breya the most artifact-synergistic commander possible.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches artifact sacrifice loops and how Breya's ability turns excess artifacts into removal
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches Breya's sacrifice loop as a decision tree: spend two mana and sacrifice two artifacts to either deal 3 damage, drain 3 life, or give a creature -4/-4 - choosing the right mode for each board state is the deck's primary skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining artifact combo and sacrifice loops on a basics page; demonstrates why the four colors without Green form the natural artifact identity in Magic.

precons.deckDescription: A Daxos-led Orzhov enchantment deck that gains experience counters whenever an enchantment enters under your control, then creates Spirit tokens with power and toughness equal to those counters. An unusual White-Black identity that combines enchantments with token generation through a scaling counter mechanic.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Experience counters from enchantment casts; Spirit token creation scaling with experience; enchantments matter; Orzhov identity
precons.mainStrategy: Cast enchantments to gain experience counters; use those counters to make progressively larger Spirit tokens; win through enchantment synergies and a growing token army

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Enchantment lovers who want a two-color Orzhov deck combining enchantments with token generation via experience counters
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players wanting a traditional Orzhov life-drain deck; the enchantment focus is specific
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Orzhov players who want an unusual enchantment angle rather than pure aristocrats or life drain

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's enchantment order and Black's underworld connection combine - Daxos trapped in Theros makes enchantments into spirits, bridging the two colors' identities
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how White-Black combines enchantment order (White) with the underworld's spiritual power (Black) through Daxos's lore - enchantments become spirits, bridging both colors' thematic identities through a unique mechanical expression.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how experience counters create a scaling engine tied to a specific card type - each enchantment grows future Spirit tokens
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches experience counters as a scaling mechanic tied to a specific card type - every enchantment cast grows future Spirit tokens, creating a deckbuilding incentive to maximize enchantment density rather than just picking the best individual cards.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining experience counters and enchantment-matters strategies on a basics page; Daxos's Spirit tokens make the connection between enchantments and combat presence visually immediate.

precons.deckDescription: A Mizzix-led Izzet spellslinger deck that gains experience counters by casting spells with CMC greater than the current experience count, reducing all instant and sorcery costs by one per counter. Snowballs quickly from a few experience counters into near-free high-impact spells. High combo ceiling.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Experience counters from high-CMC spells; cost reduction per experience counter; instant and sorcery snowball; near-free spells at high experience
precons.mainStrategy: Cast instants and sorceries to gain experience counters; use those counters to reduce spell costs, enabling increasingly explosive turns of chained high-impact spells

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Spellslinger and combo players who want to snowball experience counters into near-free high-impact spells
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Creature-focused or combat-heavy players; solitaire-feeling at high experience counts
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Izzet players who want the most spell-chain-focused Commander experience

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Izzet's spell-obsessed identity reaches its peak here - each spell cast makes future spells cheaper, until the entire deck costs almost nothing
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Izzet's spell-obsession taken to its extreme - Blue's love of optimization meets Red's passion for explosive moments as experience counters make every subsequent spell cheaper, building toward a turn where the entire deck costs almost nothing.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how experience counters compound over time, turning a spell-heavy deck into an exponentially cheaper engine
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches experience counter snowballing: the first few experience counters are hard to earn but each one makes earning the next faster - understanding this curve and protecting Mizzix through the vulnerable early turns is the critical skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining experience counters and cost reduction; Mizzix shows how early investment can create increasing late-game returns.

precons.deckDescription: A Meren-led Golgari graveyard recursion deck that gains experience counters when creatures die and reanimates creatures at end of turn based on those counters. Meren creates a recurring death-and-return loop that can generate value each turn.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Experience counters from creature deaths; end-of-turn reanimation scaling with experience; sacrifice synergies; perpetual recursion loop
precons.mainStrategy: Gain experience counters by having creatures die; use those counters to reanimate creatures at end of turn - creatures with high CMC return to battlefield, others to hand

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Golgari players who want graveyard recursion with a scaling experience-counter engine
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players in groups with heavy graveyard hate; combat-focused players who want to win more directly
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Golgari players who want a classic graveyard-recursion commander with a sacrifice loop

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Classic Golgari: Black reclaims from death, Green provides the creature bodies - Meren's experience counters turn that cycle into a perpetual machine
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Captures Golgari's life-death cycle at its most elegant - Green provides the creatures and Black reclaims them, with Meren's experience counters making that cycle increasingly efficient until death becomes cheaper than life.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how sacrifice creates a renewable death/recursion loop - death is never final with enough experience counters
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches the Golgari sacrifice loop as a self-sustaining engine: creatures die to generate experience, experience enables free recursion, recursed creatures die again for more experience - identifying the best sacrifice targets to maximize this loop is the central skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful Golgari graveyard example showing how Black and Green turn the graveyard into a resource engine rather than a discard pile.

precons.deckDescription: A Kalemne-led red-white deck built around creatures with CMC 5 or greater that earn experience counters, growing Kalemne into an increasingly powerful double-striker. It is a Giants-flavored big-creature aggro deck with an experience-counter twist.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Experience counters from 5+ CMC spells; Kalemne double strike and vigilance scaling; Giants tribal flavor; big-creature aggro
precons.mainStrategy: Play expensive creatures (CMC 5+) to earn experience counters that grow Kalemne; win through combat with double-strike, vigilance Kalemne plus an army of giants

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who want a big-creatures aggro Boros deck with a giant tribal feel and simple scaling through experience counters
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Control or combo players; described as least popular of the C15 decks but packed with powerful cards
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Boros players who want big creatures over tokens or equipment

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Red's giant-smashing aggression and White's martial order build an army of enormous threats led by a growing commander
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Boros through the lens of legendary giants - White provides the disciplined military structure and Red channels the passionate combat power, with Kalemne's experience counter growth embodying the Boros belief that battle makes warriors stronger.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Simple lesson: cast big creatures, earn experience, attack with a growing double-striker
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how experience counters reward a specific deckbuilding constraint (CMC 5+) and how Kalemne's double strike means each additional +1/+1 counter from experience doubles her damage output, creating disproportionate scaling.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining experience counters in a Boros context on a basics page; honest case study in how a color combination's limitations (card draw) can shape deck identity even within a strong mechanical framework.

precons.deckDescription: An Ezuri-led Simic experience counter deck that gains experience whenever a creature with power 2 or less enters, then dumps a number of +1/+1 counters equal to experience onto one creature each upkeep. Creates one enormously powerful threat from small utility creatures as the experience engine.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Experience counters from power-2-or-less creatures; +1/+1 counter dump equal to experience; small creatures as engine fuel; single large threat creation
precons.secondaryTheme: Small creatures enabling the experience engine
precons.mainStrategy: Play creatures with power 2 or less to gain experience counters; use those counters to dump a massive pile of +1/+1 counters onto one creature each turn - a single unblockable threat

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Simic players who want an experience-counter deck focused on growing one creature into an unstoppable threat via counter stacking
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer wide board strategies or those who dislike single-target voltron-like finishes
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Simic players who want a patient, scaling game plan centered on counter stacking

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's analytical growth and Green's natural adaptation combine in Ezuri's vision - small things become enormous through patient accumulation
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Simic's growth-through-knowledge philosophy made literal - Blue's analytical precision identifies which creature receives the counter pile, while Green's natural growth provides the small creatures that fuel the experience engine.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how small creatures can serve as engine fuel rather than threats themselves - the power is in what they enable
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how small creatures can function as pure engine fuel rather than threats - the entire early game is about deploying power-2-or-less creatures not to attack but to accumulate experience, and then choosing which single creature to make unstoppable.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining how small creatures enable large payoffs on a basics page; shows the Simic philosophy of patient investment in contrast to the more explosive Izzet or Gruul approaches.

precons.deckDescription: A Nahiri-led mono-White equipment deck featuring the Lieutenant mechanic that buffs creatures when the commander is on the battlefield. Nahiri generates tokens and tutors equipment through her planeswalker abilities. Constrained by mono-White's card draw limitations but packed with strong equipment support cards.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Equipment synergies; Lieutenant mechanic; Nahiri planeswalker as commander; token generation for equip targets; mono-White card draw constraints
precons.mainStrategy: Equip creatures with Nahiri's help, generate tokens via her planeswalker abilities, and win through combat with well-equipped creatures - hampered by mono-White's card advantage limitations

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Equipment fans interested in mono-White's unique constraints and a historically significant commander
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who expect consistent card advantage; mono-White's resource limitations make this difficult to pilot
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Pure White-identity players who want to explore equipment in mono-White's constrained but focused environment

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Mono-White's pure order and justice - equipping the chosen with legendary weapons, but limited by White's inability to draw cards effectively
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Presents mono-White's purest identity - order, protection, and equipment as the expression of White's belief in discipline and preparation, while also honestly demonstrating White's Commander limitations: card draw is a structural weakness.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Honest lesson in mono-White's strengths (structure, protection, equipment) and weaknesses (card draw) in Commander
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players that mono-color decks have structural trade-offs: Nahiri's power is real but mono-White's card draw limitations mean every card must be more efficient to compensate, which is itself a valuable deckbuilding lesson.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Valuable for explaining mono-White identity and its Commander limitations on a basics page; honest case study in how color philosophy creates both strengths and constraints.

precons.deckDescription: A Teferi-led mono-Blue deck that surprisingly focuses on big creatures - primarily sea monsters - rather than traditional Blue control. Uses the Lieutenant mechanic and ramp effects to deploy 6+ CMC threats ahead of schedule. Subverts Blue's control reputation with a creature-threat identity.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Lieutenant mechanic; sea monster tribal flavor; 6+ CMC creature focus; Teferi planeswalker as commander; mono-Blue ramp
precons.mainStrategy: Ramp into 6+ mana creatures - primarily sea monsters - and win through combat; a surprisingly creature-heavy mono-Blue deck rather than a control deck

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players curious about an unusual mono-Blue deck that subverts the typical control expectation with giant sea creatures
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players expecting a typical Blue counterspell control deck; this is a ramp-into-fatties strategy
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mono-Blue players who want to explore a non-control, creature-threat identity

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Mono-Blue's depths contain the ocean's most terrifying creatures - Teferi uses time itself to ramp into them, subverting Blue's reputation as the control color
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Subverts Blue's control reputation by revealing its hidden depth - beneath Blue's counterspell surface lies an appreciation for vast, incomprehensible threats, and Teferi's sea monsters represent Blue's relationship with the unknowable and enormous.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches that Blue doesn't have to be pure control - it can ramp into massive threats when given the right shell
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to question color assumptions: Blue doesn't have to be reactive control - it can ramp into enormous threats using temporal manipulation as mana acceleration, demonstrating the breadth of what Blue can accomplish when not constrained by archetype expectations.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for challenging color stereotypes by showing how mono-Blue can pursue a creature-based win condition.

precons.mainCommander: Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath
precons.deckDescription: An Ob Nixilis-led mono-Black Demon tribal deck featuring the Lieutenant mechanic and Ob Nixilis's Demon token generation. Combines Black's removal depth with a big-creature tribal identity centered on Demons. Flavor-forward with strong thematic resonance and solid reprints.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Lieutenant mechanic; Demon tribal; Ob Nixilis Demon token creation; mono-Black removal; big creature tribal
precons.mainStrategy: Summon an army of Demons using Ob Nixilis's abilities, support them with Black's removal, and overwhelm opponents with infernal threats

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Demon tribal fans and mono-Black players who want a flavor-driven big-creature tribal deck
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer aggressive combat or highly synergistic combo builds over a flavor-first tribal experience
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Pure Black-identity players who want a thematic demon-summoning experience

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Mono-Black at its most thematic - Ob Nixilis summons infernal armies, embodying Black's relationship with power, cost, and domination through dark means
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Embodies mono-Black's most thematic identity - Ob Nixilis summons infernal armies at the cost of life and loyalty, expressing Black's philosophy that power demands sacrifice and that even the most terrifying creatures are tools to be exploited.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Approachable flavor-first deck; teaches mono-Black identity through a classic Demon lord archetype
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how mono-Black approaches creature tribal differently from other colors - using removal and recursion as supporting tools that keep the Demon army perpetually threatening rather than relying on tribal synergies as the primary engine.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong flavor-first example for explaining mono-Black identity on a basics page; Ob Nixilis and Demon tribal make Black's philosophical relationship with power, cost, and domination immediately tangible.

precons.deckDescription: A Daretti-led mono-Red artifact recursion deck that loots to fill the graveyard with artifacts, then recurs and doubles them from the graveyard. It combines Red's destructive creativity with artifact recursion in an unusual color identity.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Artifact recursion via Daretti; looting to fill graveyard; artifact doubling from graveyard; Lieutenant mechanic; mono-Red artifacts
precons.mainStrategy: Ramp into large artifacts, sacrifice them for value, then recur them from the graveyard - Daretti's looting ability fills the graveyard while his other abilities recur artifacts

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Mono-Red artifact players who want to use sacrifice and recursion loops
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer creature-based or spell-focused Red strategies
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mono-Red players who want an artifact identity that leverages Red's love of destruction as a feature rather than a flaw

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Red's relationship with destruction and invention - artifacts aren't permanents to protect but fuel to burn and reclaim, expressing Red's impulsive creativity
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates mono-Red's most creative identity - Daretti doesn't just destroy artifacts but rebuilds them from wreckage, expressing Red's impulse-driven creativity as a cycle of destruction and reconstruction rather than permanent construction.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches artifact graveyard recursion as a Red strategy - destruction enables recursion rather than stopping it
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches artifact graveyard management as an active skill: Daretti's looting ability requires choosing which artifacts to discard intentionally for future recursion, making every loot activation a deckbuilding decision played in real time.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining mono-Red artifact strategies and how Red's relationship with destruction can become a recursion engine.

precons.deckDescription: A Freyalise-led mono-Green Elf tribal deck featuring 37 creatures (mostly Elves) that generate enormous mana quantities before closing with a massive overrun effect. The most cohesive C14 deck thematically, Freyalise's abilities directly support the Elf swarm strategy with removal and token generation.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Elf tribal; mana dork swarm; overrun win condition; Freyalise planeswalker as commander; Lieutenant mechanic; mono-Green
precons.mainStrategy: Fill the battlefield with Elves (37 creatures, mostly Elves), generate enormous amounts of mana with them, then cast a massive overrun effect to win

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Elf tribal fans and mono-Green players who want the classic Elf swarm into overrun game plan
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer non-tribal or control strategies; simple game plan may feel repetitive
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mono-Green players who want the purest expression of Green's tribal identity and mana generation

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Mono-Green at its most cohesive - Elves embody Green's principle of growth through community, generating overwhelming collective mana and force
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Presents mono-Green at its most collective and cohesive - Elves embody Green's philosophy that individual strength matters less than community power, and the Elf swarm generates mana that no individual creature could produce alone.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Most cohesive C14 tribal deck; teaches how mana dorks enable explosive turns and how overrun effects win through combat
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how Elf mana dorks function as a ramp engine rather than threats: each Elf makes the next Elf cheaper to play and the overrun effect more powerful, creating a linear but deeply satisfying acceleration curve.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful mono-Green tribal example showing how Green's community-based philosophy translates into collective mana generation.

precons.deckDescription: A Derevi-led Bant deck built around evasive flying creatures and Derevi's tap/untap triggers for light control. Derevi's unique ability to enter from the command zone for four mana bypasses commander tax entirely. Versatile enough to support stax upgrades though the precon plays as straightforward evasion.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Evasion via flying creatures; Derevi untap triggers; command zone deployment bypassing commander tax; light control elements
precons.mainStrategy: Build a small army of flying and evasive creatures, use Derevi's untap triggers for light control, and win through an unblockable creature swarm

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Bant players who want evasive combat with untap control elements; Derevi is powerful and flexible
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Playgroups that dislike stax/control; Derevi is notorious for leading oppressive decks outside the precon context
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Bant players wanting evasion-based tempo control; note Derevi's broader reputation for stax upgrades

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Bant's White order, Blue control, and Green creatures combine into a disciplined aerial assault - Derevi turns creatures into tapping/untapping control levers
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Bant's disciplined aerial identity - White organizes the flying formation, Blue provides the evasive tactical precision, and Green supplies the creature density that makes Derevi's untap triggers consistently relevant.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches evasion as a combat advantage and introduces Derevi's unique command zone ability
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how Derevi's untap triggers create a tempo advantage that compounds over multiple turns - each untapped permanent represents either free mana or a reset blocker, and identifying which permanents to untap in each situation is the deck's central skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining untap effects and tempo control on a basics page; Derevi demonstrates how passive triggers from combat can accumulate into a decisive advantage without requiring any additional mana investment.

precons.deckDescription: An Oloro-led Esper life gain deck where Oloro generates life, card draw, and opponent life loss from the command zone without ever being cast. The passive command zone engine makes Oloro unique - he functions as an always-on enchantment that fuels an artifact and life-gain strategy.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Passive life gain from command zone; Oloro card draw trigger; opponent life loss drain; artifact subtheme; life gain payoffs
precons.secondaryTheme: Artifacts / eminence-style life gain from command zone
precons.mainStrategy: Gain life every upkeep via Oloro's command zone ability, convert life gain into card draw and damage, and use an artifact subtheme for additional value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Life gain enthusiasts who want Esper's control tools paired with a passive life engine from the command zone
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Aggressive or combat-focused players; Oloro is a slow, inevitability-based strategy
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Esper players who want a passive life-gain engine that enables card draw and life-based payoffs

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Esper's White permanence, Blue knowledge, and Black ambition converge - Oloro's eternal life fuels a slow but inevitable advantage engine
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Esper's most passive expression of inevitability - Oloro's command zone ability generates life, card draw, and damage every turn without being cast, teaching players that Black and Blue's resource accumulation doesn't always require active plays.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how life gain becomes a resource engine when converted into cards and damage via Oloro's triggered abilities
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how passive resource generation compounds over a long game: Oloro draws cards and drains opponents every upkeep from the command zone, creating a life/card differential that grows insurmountable if left unchecked.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining command-zone abilities and passive resource engines through a commander that can affect the game without being cast.

precons.deckDescription: A Jeleva-led Grixis deck that exiles cards from opponents' libraries when cast and allows free casting of those instants and sorceries. Recasting Jeleva with more mana exiles more cards. Nekusar (the wheel commander) and True-Name Nemesis are the most notable secondary cards.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Exile and free cast opponents' instants and sorceries; scaling exile with cast mana; Jeleva scaling commander tax; high-CMC spell focus
precons.mainStrategy: Cast Jeleva by paying large amounts of mana to exile more opponent cards; cast those cards for free; escalate with each recast of Jeleva

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Experienced spellslinger players who want to exploit opponent spells; Nekusar secondary commander is the more popular build
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Beginners; the free spell mechanic requires understanding of exile zones and scaling commander cost
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Grixis players interested in spell theft and escalating resource exploitation

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Grixis's Blue cunning steals knowledge, Black exploits it, and Red casts it explosively - using opponents' best spells against them
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Embodies Grixis's opportunistic resource philosophy - Blue steals knowledge, Black exploits it ruthlessly, and Red casts it explosively; Jeleva's exile-and-cast mechanic turns opponents' best spells into Grixis's most powerful weapons.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches scaling commander cost mechanics and exile-zone casting for advanced players
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches scaling commander cost strategy: casting Jeleva with more mana exiles more cards, creating an incentive to delay the first cast until enough mana is available to exile the most valuable opponent spells.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good advanced example for explaining exile casting and scaling commander cost on a basics page; demonstrates Grixis's philosophy of turning opponent resources against them.

precons.deckDescription: A Prossh-led Jund sacrifice deck that generates Kobold tokens equal to the mana spent to cast it, scaling with each recast. Those tokens become immediate sacrifice fodder for Food Chain or other payoffs. Beloved at every power level from casual aristocrats to near-cEDH with Food Chain.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Kobold token scaling with cast mana; sacrifice loop with Food Chain potential; Prossh commander tax scaling; aristocrats to cEDH spectrum
precons.mainStrategy: Cast Prossh generating Kobold tokens equal to mana spent; sacrifice those tokens for Food Chain or other payoffs; recast for more tokens and escalating power

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Competitive-leaning players; Prossh is beloved as a casual-to-cEDH scaling commander with Food Chain combo potential
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Casual players who dislike being targeted; Prossh is notorious at every power level
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Jund players who want the highest-ceiling sacrifice commander from this era

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Jund's Black sacrifice, Red aggression, and Green ramp combine perfectly - Prossh literally makes tokens from mana spent to sacrifice immediately
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Captures Jund's most explosive identity - Green generates the mana, Black provides the sacrifice willingness, and Red drives the aggression; Prossh converts all three into a Kobold token flood that scales with each recast.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not for beginners - teaches scaling commander cost, token sacrifice loops, and Food Chain combo potential
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches scaling commander cost as a strategic advantage: each Prossh recast generates more tokens than the last, and understanding how Food Chain converts those tokens into infinite mana is the deck's ceiling - the precon teaches the floor while pointing toward the sky.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining scaling token generation and sacrifice loops on a basics page; Prossh demonstrates how Jund's three colors combine into the highest-ceiling sacrifice commander in Commander history.

precons.deckDescription: A Marath-led Naya deck with a flexible commander that enters with +1/+1 counters equal to mana spent and can ping, make tokens, or pump creatures. Beast tribal flavor with limited Beast-specific synergies at time of printing. Marath's scaling ability rewards replaying the commander for growing versatility.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Marath scaling with commander cost; three-mode activated ability (ping/token/pump); Beast tribal flavor; +1/+1 counter scaling
precons.mainStrategy: Cast Marath to enter with counters equal to mana spent; use those counters to ping, make tokens, or pump creatures; scale counters with each recast

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Naya players who want a flexible commander with scaling power and a beast tribal flavor
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players seeking strong tribal payoffs; Beast synergies were sparse in 2013 and the deck lacks dedicated Beast payoffs
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Naya players who value commander flexibility and counter scaling over focused tribal synergy

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Naya's White order, Red wildness, and Green beast-power combine in Marath - a primal force that grows with each summoning
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Naya's wildest identity - White marshals the beast army in formation, Red channels primal aggression, and Green supplies the raw creature power; Marath's three-mode ability gives each color a distinct mechanical expression.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how scaling commander cost creates a growing mana sink with three different modes - flexibility as a resource
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches flexibility as a strategic resource: Marath's three modes (ping, token, pump) mean the optimal play changes every turn based on board state, training players to evaluate which mode generates the most value in each specific situation.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining flexible commanders and scaling with cast cost on a basics page; Marath demonstrates how a single ability with three modes can adapt to any game state.

precons.deckDescription: The original Mardu precon led by Kaalia of the Vast, who puts an Angel, Demon, or Dragon from hand into play whenever she attacks. The deck enables a multi-tribe strategy across three creature types and often makes Kaalia a high-priority removal target.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Free Angel/Demon/Dragon deployment on attack; multi-tribe (Angels, Demons, Dragons); combat attack trigger; Join Forces and Vow cycle mechanics
precons.primaryTheme: Angels, Demons, Dragons tribal (cheating into play)
precons.mainStrategy: Attack with Kaalia to put an Angel, Demon, or Dragon from hand into play for free; build a board of enormous flying threats via repeated combat triggers

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who love big flying threats across three iconic creature types and want to cheat expensive creatures into play via combat
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer slower or non-combat strategies; Kaalia is a high-priority removal target every game
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mardu players who want a combat-first, big-creature identity across three iconic creature types

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Mardu's White righteousness (Angels), Black darkness (Demons), and Red fire (Dragons) unite under Kaalia - combining all three divine/infernal creature types into one aggressive identity
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Embodies Mardu's most epic identity - White's righteous Angels, Black's infernal Demons, and Red's primal Dragons united under Kaalia, expressing how Mardu's three colors each command a different legendary flying creature type.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Classic beginner-to-intermediate lesson: Kaalia cheats mana costs - protect her to get free threats; teaches attack trigger dependency
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches attack trigger dependency as a strategic vulnerability: Kaalia's power requires connecting with combat damage, making her the highest-priority removal target every game - protecting Kaalia and creating windows to attack safely is the critical skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining attack triggers and multi-tribe strategies through a commander whose attack trigger defines the deck's plan.

precons.deckDescription: A Riku-led Temur deck that copies both spells and creatures through Riku's two abilities, doubling the impact of every large spell or creature cast. Requires significant mana investment to activate copy abilities. Often described as unfocused out of the box but powerful with upgrades.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Spell copying via Riku; creature copying via Riku; high mana investment for copies; Temur ramp enabling copy activations; Join Forces and Vow cycle
precons.secondaryTheme: Ramp into big threats to copy
precons.mainStrategy: Ramp heavily to generate enough mana for Riku's copy abilities; cast large spells or creatures and pay Riku's ability to copy them for double the impact

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Temur players who want to double up on their best spells and creatures with Riku's copy abilities
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a focused game plan; the deck requires significant upgrades to perform consistently - noted as unfocused out of the box
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Temur players drawn to spell doubling and creature copying over direct aggro

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Temur's Green ramp, Blue copy magic, and Red big spells create an engine that doubles every investment - every mana spent gives twice the value
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Temur's doubling identity - Green ramps to enable Riku's expensive copy abilities, Blue selects which spell or creature is worth doubling, and Red provides the impulsive power of the things being doubled.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how Riku's copy abilities require mana investment and sequencing - understanding when to copy versus just casting
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches mana investment decision-making: Riku's copy abilities cost one additional mana each, creating a constant decision between casting something powerful or copying something already cast - understanding when to copy versus when to advance the board is the central skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining copy effects and mana investment decisions on a basics page; Riku demonstrates how Temur can build a value engine around doubling rather than through raw creature power.

precons.deckDescription: A Ghave-led Abzan deck combining +1/+1 counters, token generation, and sacrifice in a single commander whose abilities enable all three strategies simultaneously. Ghave can both spend counters to make tokens and spend tokens to make counters, creating a self-sustaining engine with high combo ceiling.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Ghave token-from-counter and counter-from-token duality; sacrifice synergies; +1/+1 counter manipulation; flexible win conditions; Join Forces and Vow cycle
precons.mainStrategy: Build a swarm of small tokens loaded with +1/+1 counters via Ghave; overrun opponents with the army or sacrifice tokens for value - often both simultaneously

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Abzan players who want a flexible commander that supports counters, tokens, and sacrifice simultaneously - with strong combo potential
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a simple, linear game plan; Ghave's flexibility can make decision-making overwhelming
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Abzan players who want the most flexible +1/+1 counter commander, capable of multiple win lines

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Abzan's White tokens, Black sacrifice, and Green growth combine in Ghave - a deck where every game piece serves double duty as both threat and fuel
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows Abzan's most versatile identity - White generates the token community, Black extracts sacrifice value from it, and Green provides the growth counters that make those tokens increasingly powerful before they're sacrificed.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how a single commander ability creates multiple viable game plans - Ghave's flexibility is both its strength and its complexity
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches Ghave's self-referential loop: spending a counter creates a token, sacrificing a token puts a counter back - recognizing that this loop can be entered with any additional mana or effect that puts counters or creates tokens is the deck's highest-level skill.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining token-counter combo loops and how two simple abilities can create a self-sustaining loop with the right support.

precons.deckDescription: A Zedruu-led Jeskai politics deck that donates permanents - ideally harmful ones - to opponents, then draws cards and gains life for each donated permanent each upkeep. Requires creative deckbuilding to find permanents worth giving away. One of the most unusual and skill-testing Commander precons ever made.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Permanent donation for life gain and card draw; cursed gift strategy; pillowfort elements; Zedruu upkeep triggers; Join Forces and Vow cycle
precons.secondaryTheme: Life gain and card draw from donated permanents
precons.mainStrategy: Give permanents - ideally harmful ones - to opponents; gain life and draw cards equal to donated permanents per upkeep; win through pillowfort and political maneuvering

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Political players who enjoy donating harmful permanents and winning through a pillowfort while others fight over cursed gifts
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a reliable win condition; the deck lacks an obvious finisher and requires experience to pilot effectively
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Jeskai players who want maximum political gameplay; a unique and polarizing experience

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Jeskai's White fairness twisted by Red's chaos and Blue's manipulation - gifts are traps, generosity is a weapon, and the table is the deck's battlefield
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates Jeskai's most subversive identity - White's apparent generosity masks Blue's calculated strategy and Red's chaotic gift-giving; Zedruu's donation mechanic weaponizes all three colors' relationship with sharing.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Not for beginners - teaches advanced political concepts: what to give, when to give it, and how to build a life/card advantage engine from donations
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches donation strategy as a two-part skill: first, finding permanents worth giving away (curses, harmful enchantments, useless tokens); second, protecting yourself with a pillowfort while Zedruu's upkeep accumulates life and cards - both halves must work together.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful for explaining political donation strategies and how apparent generosity can support a win condition when the gifts are carefully chosen.

precons.deckDescription: A Mimeoplasm-led Sultai graveyard deck that casts The Mimeoplasm to combine two creatures in the graveyard - one for abilities, one for power - into one enormous hybrid threat. Self-mill fills the graveyard with desirable combination targets. The original Sultai graveyard commander precon.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Mimeoplasm graveyard combination; self-mill to fill graveyard; power/ability split targeting; flexible threat construction; Join Forces and Vow cycle
precons.mainStrategy: Fill the graveyard with creatures that have interesting abilities and creatures with high power/toughness; cast The Mimeoplasm to combine the best of both into one enormous threat

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Sultai graveyard players who want a flexible commander that combines multiple threats into one overwhelmingly powerful creature
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike graveyard-dependent strategies or those who face heavy graveyard hate
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Sultai players who want the original graveyard-combination commander from the first precon release

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Sultai's Black graveyard dominion, Green's enormous creatures, and Blue's self-mill create the perfect hunting ground for The Mimeoplasm - every dead creature is a potential power upgrade
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Captures Sultai's graveyard philosophy - Black fills it and reclaims from it, Blue selects which creatures to target for combination, and Green provides the enormous power values that make The Mimeoplasm's combined form devastating.
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches graveyard deckbuilding - selecting creatures that pair well as Mimeoplasm targets (ability + power) is a fundamental deckbuilding lesson
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches graveyard deckbuilding with a specific dual-target goal: identifying creatures with the best abilities (for the Mimeoplasm to copy) and creatures with the highest power (for the Mimeoplasm to take counters from) - these are often different cards.
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful Sultai graveyard example teaching that creatures can fill distinct copy and counter roles in the same deck.

precons.deckDescription: A Strefan-led Rakdos Vampire deck focused on cheating large Vampires into play rather than token flooding. Strefan's attack trigger lets you put a Vampire from hand into play for free if Blood tokens were created this turn. A bigger-creature approach that distinguishes it from Edgar Markov.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Strefan attack trigger for free Vampire deployment; Blood token generation; big Vampire focus over token flooding; Vampire tribal
precons.primaryTheme: Vampire tribal / cheating big Vampires into play
precons.mainStrategy: Use Strefan's Sneak Attack-style ability to put large Vampires into play for free; focus on bigger Vampires rather than token flooding

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Vampire fans who want a bigger-creatures approach rather than token flooding; players who enjoy Sneak Attack-style cheating in Rakdos colors
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players expecting Edgar Markov's wide token strategy; those who dislike combat-dependent commanders
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Rakdos players drawn to Black's ambition and Red's aggression - putting enormous Vampires into play for free embodies both colors' love of paying any cost for power

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black's hunger for dominance and Red's impulsive aggression merge in Strefan - why cast expensive Vampires when you can simply take them from your hand and throw them into battle?
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows that Vampire decks don't have to flood with tokens - Black and Red together can pursue a big-threat, high-impact path that rewards patience and a well-stocked hand
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how attack triggers generate value beyond combat damage - Strefan's ability turns each attack into a free creature deployment
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches hand management around Strefan: keeping high-impact Vampires in hand for free deployment is more important than playing them out normally
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of a Vampire deck that defies the typical token-flood expectation; useful for showing Rakdos tribal identity

precons.deckDescription: A Millicent-led Azorius Spirit tribal deck that creates Spirit tokens when Spirits deal combat damage and leverages Millicent's ETB and attack triggers to build a wide flying board. A clean go-wide evasion strategy using White-Blue's natural affinity for Spirit tribal.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Millicent Spirit token generation on ETB and combat; Spirit tribal flying synergies; go-wide evasive combat; White-Blue Spirit identity
precons.mainStrategy: Build a wide board of Spirits quickly using tribal synergies; go-wide combat strategy in Azorius colors

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Spirit tribal fans and players who want a clean, approachable go-wide strategy in Azorius colors
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a complex or combo-heavy experience; those who find token go-wide strategies repetitive
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Azorius players who value White's token structure and Blue's evasive flight - a disciplined aerial Spirit force that wins cleanly through combat

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White creates the token army and protects it with structure, while Blue provides the evasion and card selection that ensures the Spirit swarm is always relevant
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Azorius approaches tribal - not through brute force but through evasion, protection, and precise token deployment
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Accessible introduction to Spirit tribal and go-wide flying strategies; teaches how evasion converts token quantity into consistent damage
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to leverage evasive tribal creatures to maintain consistent damage output that opponents struggle to interact with
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Clean Azorius tribal example; good for explaining how White and Blue combine tokens with evasion for a distinctive go-wide identity

precons.deckDescription: A Wilhelt-led Dimir Zombie tribal deck that draws a card and creates a Decayed Zombie token when a non-token Zombie dies under your control. The self-replacing token mechanic makes the board remarkably resilient, converting each Zombie death into continued board presence and card advantage.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Wilhelt death trigger; Decayed Zombie token replacement on non-token Zombie death; Zombie tribal card draw; graveyard interaction
precons.mainStrategy: Build a Zombie horde in Dimir colors; includes key Zombie reprints; Wilhelt generates value when Zombies die and creates token replacements

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Zombie tribal fans who want a Dimir twist on the classic archetype with graveyard depth and token self-replacement
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players wanting a completely novel experience; Zombie tribal is well-trodden territory and this deck doesn't dramatically reinvent it
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Dimir players who want Black's graveyard dominion over Zombies combined with Blue's selective card draw and graveyard management - the thinking Zombie player

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black commands the undead army while Blue curates it - Wilhelt ensures no Zombie truly dies, replacing each loss with a Decayed token and turning death into a resource
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Blue adds a layer of strategic graveyard management to Black's Zombie identity - death becomes a revolving door rather than a permanent loss
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Good entry-level tribal deck; Wilhelt's Decayed token replacement teaches players how sacrifice and death triggers create self-sustaining loops
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how token replacement mechanics create resilient board states and how Decayed tokens enable sacrifice synergies without losing board presence
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Solid Dimir Zombie example; useful for explaining how Black-Blue approaches tribal differently from mono-Black through graveyard selectivity

precons.deckDescription: A Leinore-led Selesnya +1/+1 counter deck built around the Coven mechanic, which requires three creatures with different power values for maximum payoffs. Leinore adds a +1/+1 counter to a creature and draws a card at end of combat when Coven is active. Backup commander Kyler supports a Human tribal alternate route.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Coven mechanic requiring three different power values; +1/+1 counter distribution on Coven activation; Leinore card draw at end of combat; Kyler Human tribal backup
precons.secondaryTheme: Coven mechanic / Human tribal (via backup commander Kyler)
precons.mainStrategy: Distribute +1/+1 counters to meet Coven requirements (three creatures with different power); backup commander Kyler supports Human tribal route

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Counter enthusiasts who want a Selesnya deck with a mechanical twist; players interested in the Coven mechanic and Human tribal via the backup commander
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a single focused game plan; Coven's requirement for three different power values adds a constraint that can be awkward to maintain
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Selesnya players who value White's community and Green's growth - Coven rewards having a diverse creature board rather than stacking one threat, reflecting both colors' group-oriented philosophy

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's diversity-in-unity and Green's natural growth combine in Coven - rewarding a board that looks like a community rather than a single dominant force
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Illustrates how Selesnya can approach +1/+1 counters not as a stacking game but as a precision tool for maintaining specific power thresholds
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches the Coven mechanic and how power-level differentiation matters beyond just making creatures bigger - sometimes diversity is the engine
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to deliberately manage creature power values rather than simply buffing everything equally - a unique constraint-based deckbuilding lesson
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of a Selesnya counter deck with a mechanical constraint; useful for explaining Coven and how Midnight Hunt's design tied mechanics to flavor

precons.productSection: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms Commander
precons.deckDescription: A Galea-led Bant Aura and Equipment deck that allows casting of Auras and Equipment directly off the top of the library for free. Galea solves the card disadvantage problem of Aura strategies by replacing each enchantment as it's cast. A hybrid voltron deck combining both attachment types.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Free top-of-library casting of Auras and Equipment; Aura card disadvantage mitigation; Equipment and Aura hybrid; voltron combat strategy
precons.mainStrategy: Pump up Galea or one creature with Auras and Equipment; Galea lets you cast those spells off the top of your library for free, enabling a library-top-play enchantress-equipment hybrid

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Aura and Equipment fans who want both in a single Bant deck; players who enjoy casting permanents off the top of their library as a card advantage engine
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a pure voltron experience; the dual Aura/Equipment focus can dilute both strategies if not built carefully
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Bant players who value Blue's knowledge and planning, White's protective enchantments, and Green's creature base - Galea embodies the Bant ideal of well-equipped, well-protected threats

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's top-of-library manipulation, White's Aura protection, and Green's creature power combine to make Galea a fully self-sufficient voltron commander who draws and deploys simultaneously
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Bant colors unify two traditionally separate strategies (Auras and Equipment) through Blue's library manipulation, making them work as one cohesive engine
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how library-top casting removes the card disadvantage problem that normally plagues Aura strategies - Galea draws and plays simultaneously
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches the core Aura vulnerability lesson (two-for-one risk) and how Galea's ability mitigates it by replacing the card as it's played
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example for explaining the Aura card-disadvantage problem and how a commander ability can solve it; good Bant identity showcase

precons.productSection: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms Commander
precons.deckDescription: A Vrondiss-led Gruul Dragon tribal deck that triggers Enrage to create 5/4 Dragon Spirit tokens whenever Vrondiss takes damage. Multiple strong backup commanders (Klauth for mana, Wulfgar for trigger doubling) provide alternate aggressive lines.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Enrage on damage to create Dragon Spirit tokens; Dragon tribal combat focus; Klauth extra mana on attack; Wulfgar attack trigger doubling; dice rolling subtheme
precons.mainStrategy: Make big Dragons and attack; Vrondiss triggers Enrage to create Dragon Spirit tokens; backup commanders Klauth and Wulfgar offer alternate aggressive lines

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Dragon fans who want a Gruul deck with combat aggression and a clear, satisfying game plan; players who enjoy multiple strong backup commander options
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a unique or unusual Dragon deck; this is a straightforward attack-with-Dragons strategy without much complexity
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Gruul players who embody Red's dragon-fire aggression and Green's overwhelming creature power - the most direct expression of Gruul's combat identity

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Red's primal dragon energy and Green's unstoppable creature force merge in Vrondiss - Enrage turns damage into more Dragons, and more Dragons mean more damage
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Gruul combines Red's love of Dragons with Green's ramp to consistently produce the largest creatures on the board earlier than any other color pair
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Very accessible: ramp with Green, cast Dragons with Red, attack with everything. The Enrage trigger teaches players to turn damage into advantage rather than just a cost
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how Enrage creates a damage-into-value loop and how backup commanders (Klauth, Wulfgar) offer dramatically different aggressive lines from the same base deck
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong beginner-accessible example for Dragon tribal and Gruul identity; good for showing how backup commanders can shift a deck's entire identity

precons.productSection: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms Commander
precons.deckDescription: A Sefris-led Esper Venture into the Dungeon deck that reanimates a creature card when a dungeon is completed. Venture triggers advance through three dungeon options with escalating rewards, and completion triggers Sefris's recursion ability.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Venture into the Dungeon mechanic; dungeon completion triggers Sefris reanimation; three dungeon options with escalating rewards; graveyard recursion backup
precons.mainStrategy: Progress through Dungeon cards via Venture triggers; Sefris reanimates creatures when you complete a dungeon; flexible into alternate strategies if dungeon support is insufficient

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players curious about the Venture into the Dungeon mechanic and fans of the D&D flavor; those who enjoy reanimation as a backup win condition
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a mechanically tight, focused deck; Venture support was limited at release and the deck can feel inconsistent without upgrades
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Esper players who value Blue's exploration of the unknown, White's structure, and Black's power over death - Sefris's dungeon-completion reanimation fits Black's graveyard identity with a D&D twist

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Esper's White structure sets the dungeon path, Blue's curiosity drives the exploration, and Black collects the reward at the end - dungeon completion as a metaphor for Esper's methodical approach to power
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Introduces the Venture mechanic and teaches players how progressive dungeon completion creates cumulative rewards - a lesson in patience and incremental value building
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches the Venture mechanic and how dungeon rooms create a sequential decision tree; also introduces reanimation as a flexible backup plan
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players how to evaluate dungeon room choices based on current game state and how reanimation can close games independently of the dungeon strategy
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining Venture into the Dungeon and how dungeon mechanics work

precons.productSection: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms Commander
precons.deckDescription: A Prosper-led Rakdos impulse-draw deck that creates a Treasure token whenever a spell is cast from exile. It combines Cascade, Madness, Adventures, and other exile-cast mechanics to trigger Prosper's ability repeatedly.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Prosper Treasure generation on exile cast; impulse draw as primary card advantage; Cascade and Madness as exile-cast enablers; self-funding Treasure engine
precons.mainStrategy: Exile cards and cast them from exile; Prosper generates Treasure tokens each time you cast a spell from exile; rewards Cascade, Madness, Adventures and other exile-cast mechanics

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy impulse draw and exile-casting strategies; those who want a Rakdos value deck that generates Treasure tokens as a byproduct of its main strategy
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer drawing cards to hand and playing them normally; impulse draw requires a different mental model of resource management
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Rakdos players who want Black's resource exploitation and Red's impulsive casting combined - Prosper embodies both colors' relationship with temporary, use-it-now resources

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black's hunger for every available resource meets Red's impulse to act immediately - Prosper turns every exiled card into a Treasure, monetizing the very act of casting from exile
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how exile functions as a second hand in Rakdos colors, and how Treasure tokens created by casting from exile create a self-funding value engine
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches impulse draw as a distinct card advantage paradigm - use it this turn or lose it, which trains players to evaluate tempo vs value in real time
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build around exile casting by including Cascade, Madness, Adventures, and other exile-enabling mechanics as mutually reinforcing engine pieces
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining impulse draw and how Treasure tokens function as mana acceleration in a Rakdos shell

precons.deckDescription: The official Commander 2021 Lorehold deck led by Osgir, the Reconstructor. Osgir makes this product a specific artifact sacrifice-and-reconstruction route, not a universal Lorehold mechanic.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Artifact sacrifice for graveyard token copies via Osgir; artifact recursion and copying.
precons.mainStrategy: Sacrifice artifacts for value, then use Osgir to turn artifact cards in the graveyard into reconstructed token copies.

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Artifact players who enjoy graveyard artifact recursion with token-copy payoffs
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players wanting traditional Boros aggro; this deck plays nothing like a typical Red-White combat deck
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Osgir turns artifact sacrifice and graveyard cards into a commander-specific reconstruction engine.

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's orderly artifact construction and Red's creative destruction combine in Osgir - nothing is wasted, everything sacrificed is doubled and returned, making the battlefield a perpetual forge
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how a commander can express Boros through artifact recursion and combo lines rather than only through aggression
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches artifact sacrifice and recursion in a clean two-color context; Osgir's doubling ability is intuitive and makes the payoff of sacrificing artifacts immediately visible
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how artifact sacrifice feeds recursion which enables further sacrifice - a self-sustaining loop that generates value every turn without needing external draw engines
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: A focused example of how a commander can turn artifact sacrifice and graveyard cards into a reconstruction engine.

precons.deckDescription: A Breena-led Orzhov political deck that adds two +1/+1 counters to Breena whenever a player other than you is attacked, and lets that attacker draw a card. It creates a political engine where Breena grows while you encourage opponents to attack each other.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Breena +1/+1 counter growth when others attacked; opponent card draw incentive; political attack redirection
precons.primaryTheme: Politics / encouraging opponents to attack each other
precons.mainStrategy: Trick opponents into attacking each other; Breena grows with +1/+1 counters whenever a player other than you is attacked; swoop in for the kill once opponents are depleted

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Political players who enjoy encouraging opponents to fight each other; those who want an Orzhov deck built around multiplayer dynamics rather than pure aggro or life drain
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer direct, aggressive strategies or those who dislike the unpredictability of relying on opponent behavior
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Orzhov players who use White's social structure and Black's manipulation to engineer the table - Breena rewards letting others fight while quietly growing into an unblockable threat

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's moral authority and Black's cunning ambition combine in Breena - she appears generous in letting others attack freely, but every skirmish that doesn't target you makes her more dangerous
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Orzhov can approach Commander's political landscape with subtlety - growing a commander while others deplete each other is a distinct and rewarding play pattern
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches political awareness in Commander: tracking who is attacking whom and how to position yourself as the least threatening player while growing the most powerful one
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to read the table, incentivize non-threatening behavior through Breena's counter triggers, and time the kill precisely when opponents are depleted
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent for explaining the political dimension of Commander and how Orzhov can win through manipulation rather than direct aggression

precons.deckDescription: A Willowdusk-led Golgari life-total-as-resource deck that converts the difference between life gained and life lost per turn into +1/+1 counters. The greater the life swing in a single turn, the more counters Willowdusk generates. Rewards deliberately cycling life totals for maximum counter production.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Life total as resource; Willowdusk counter generation from life swings; life gain and loss payoffs; deliberate life cycling strategy
precons.secondaryTheme: Life gain and life loss payoffs
precons.mainStrategy: Spend life aggressively to power effects; earn it back with life gain; Willowdusk converts life total changes into +1/+1 counters on creatures

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy using life total as a flexible resource; those who want a Golgari deck that rewards both spending and gaining life for powerful payoffs
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want to maximize life total as a defensive buffer; this deck deliberately drains and refills life rather than protecting it
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Golgari players who see life as a currency rather than a safety net - Black's willingness to spend it for power and Green's ability to replenish it create a uniquely sustainable engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black treats life as a resource to spend recklessly, while Green ensures there's always more to draw from - Willowdusk converts the fluctuation itself into +1/+1 counters, making volatility the engine
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Golgari can build a life-as-resource economy where both gaining and losing life are productive actions rather than simple buffs or costs
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches that life total is a resource, not just a number to protect - Willowdusk's ability makes players comfortable spending life aggressively, a fundamental advanced concept
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to maximize Willowdusk's counter generation by deliberately cycling through life loss and gain in the same turn for exponential counter stacking
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining life-as-resource philosophy and how Golgari approaches the life total differently from White-based life gain decks

precons.deckDescription: An Adrix and Nev-led Simic token doubling deck with a Parallel Lives effect in the command zone. Every token-generating effect produces twice as many tokens while Adrix and Nev are in play. A straightforward but exponentially powerful engine that scales every token producer in the deck.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Token doubling via Adrix and Nev Parallel Lives effect; Fractal token generation; all token producers doubled; Simic go-wide exponential scaling
precons.mainStrategy: Put a Parallel Lives in the command zone - Adrix and Nev double all tokens created; generate as many tokens as possible and win through overwhelming board presence

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Token players who want a Simic deck that doubles all token production; players who enjoy exponential board development
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a nuanced, interactive experience; this deck can feel like a solitaire engine once Adrix and Nev resolve
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Simic players who want Green's creature abundance and Blue's mathematical doubling combined into a self-multiplying token engine - the most direct expression of Simic's growth-through-knowledge identity

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's mathematical duplication and Green's natural proliferation combine in Adrix and Nev - a Parallel Lives in the command zone that makes every token producer twice as powerful
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how a single commander ability that doubles a fundamental game action (token creation) scales every card in the deck without requiring synergy-specific cards
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches the concept of multiplicative vs additive value - doubling token production is exponentially more powerful than adding more token producers
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to evaluate token producers by their output per mana and how doubling effects make even modest token generators into game-warping threats
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Excellent example of how a doubling commander creates exponential value; ideal for explaining why Parallel Lives effects are so powerful in Commander

precons.deckDescription: A Zaffai-led Izzet big-spells deck that scries 2 and creates a 4/4 Elemental token when casting spells with CMC 5+, then copies a random instant or sorcery for spells with CMC 10+. Rewards casting the most expensive spells possible for escalating trigger rewards.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: CMC-based payoffs via Zaffai; 4/4 Elemental token for 5+ CMC; spell copy for 10+ CMC; scry 2 on all instants and sorceries
precons.mainStrategy: Cast the largest instants and sorceries possible; Zaffai creates tokens and scries based on spell CMC, rewarding high-cost spells with escalating payoffs

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Spellslinger players who want a Strixhaven deck with scaling payoffs for casting the biggest possible instants and sorceries
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer creature combat or board presence strategies; this deck is primarily a spell-value engine
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Izzet players who want the full spell-magnitude experience - Blue's precision scaling and Red's explosive high-cost spells create a deck where every big spell compounds into bigger payoffs
