learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue's love of optimization meets Red's addiction to dramatic, high-cost moments - Zaffai rewards the biggest spells with the biggest tokens and scry, making mana investment directly proportional to reward
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Izzet's spellslinger identity scales from small cantrips to game-ending explosions when spell CMC is treated as a resource rather than just a cost
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches CMC as a strategic variable - deliberately casting the highest-cost spells unlocks the best Zaffai triggers, training players to think about spell selection beyond raw effect
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches players to build toward a critical mass of ramp and cheap cantrips that enable casting one massive spell per turn for maximum Zaffai trigger value
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining mana-value payoffs and a spectacle-focused Izzet spellslinger identity

precons.deckDescription: A Ranar-led Azorius Foretell deck that creates a 1/1 Spirit token whenever a card is exiled from hand or a spell is exiled as it resolves. Pairs Foretell's exile mechanic with blink effects to generate a constant stream of Spirit tokens and ETB value.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Foretell exile triggers; Spirit token on exile from hand; blink and flicker synergies; Ranar Spirit token generation
precons.mainStrategy: Foretell cards to exile them; Ranar creates Spirit tokens whenever cards are exiled from hand or resolved spells are exiled; flicker synergies extend ETB value

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy the Foretell mechanic and want an Azorius deck that rewards exile-zone interaction with blink synergies
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want aggressive or combat-heavy strategies; this deck is deliberate and value-focused
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Azorius players who value Blue's information control and White's protective structure - Foretell's exile interaction and Spirit token generation fit both colors' methodical, evasive identity

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's patient defense and Blue's hidden information combine in Ranar - cards exiled through Foretell become free Spirit tokens, turning caution into a board presence
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Introduces Foretell as a mana-smoothing and information-hiding mechanic, and shows how exile interaction creates unexpected token synergies
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Foretell as a two-turn planning mechanic - paying now to cast cheaper later trains players to think ahead about resource allocation
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to combine Foretell with blink effects for an engine that generates Spirit tokens, resets ETBs, and accumulates hand-exile advantage simultaneously
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining the Foretell mechanic and how exile-zone interaction creates token-generation payoffs

precons.deckDescription: A Lathril-led Golgari Elf tribal deck that builds toward Lathril's tap ability: tap ten Elves to drain each opponent for ten life simultaneously. A mana-dork-heavy swarm strategy with a non-combat mass life drain win condition that bypasses defensive boards entirely.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Elf tribal mana dorks; Lathril tap-ten-Elves drain ability; mass life drain win condition; go-wide swarm strategy
precons.secondaryTheme: Life drain via Lathril's tap ability
precons.mainStrategy: Build a wide board of Elves; use Lathril's tap ability (requiring 10 Elves) to drain each opponent for 10 life simultaneously for a massive life swing win

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Elf tribal fans who want a Golgari take on the archetype with a powerful mass-drain win condition via Lathril
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer combat-based wins; Lathril's tap ability requires 10 Elves and bypasses combat entirely, which can feel non-interactive
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Golgari players who want Green's explosive Elf mana generation combined with Black's drain-and-dominate win condition - a patient build toward a devastating life-swap moment

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green builds the Elf swarm and floods the battlefield, while Black weaponizes their collective presence into a life-draining tap ability that simultaneously kills opponents and sustains you
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Golgari approaches tribal differently from Selesnya or mono-Green - the Elf army is the engine, but Black provides the non-combat kill condition that closes the game
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches mana dork sequencing and how Elf synergies compound - each Elf makes the next one cheaper or more powerful, creating a snowball effect that's easy to understand
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build toward Lathril's 10-Elf threshold and how to protect that board state from sweepers using Black's resilience tools
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Classic Elf tribal example in Golgari; excellent for explaining how Black adds a non-combat win condition to Green's creature-based strategy

precons.deckDescription: An Aesi-led Simic lands deck that draws a card whenever a land enters under your control, combined with extra land plays per turn. The purest expression of Simic's ramp-and-draw identity, Aesi converts every land drop into a card and every card into more land drops.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Card draw on land entry via Aesi; extra land plays per turn; landfall-adjacent triggers; Simic ramp and draw engine
precons.mainStrategy: Play extra lands each turn; Aesi draws a card whenever a land enters under your control; build massive card and mana advantage through repeated land drops

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Land strategy and Simic value players who want the simplest and most reliable version of the lands-matter archetype
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players looking for a unique or complex experience; this is a clean but straightforward Simic value deck without many surprises
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Simic players who want Green's land acceleration and Blue's card draw joined in a 'more lands, more cards' engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green's land-as-power philosophy and Blue's card-draw engine combine perfectly - every land drop draws a card, every card draw finds more lands, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of abundance
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates the core Simic loop: ramp into lands, draw cards off those lands, find more lands - showing why this engine is so consistently powerful in Commander
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Ideal beginner's Simic deck: the game plan is simple and visible - play lands, draw cards, play more lands. The loop is easy to understand and satisfying to execute
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how extra land plays compound over multiple turns and how Aesi's trigger converts each land drop into card advantage that accelerates the entire game plan
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful entry-level Simic example showing how Green ramp and Blue card draw combine into a value engine

precons.deckDescription: A Wyleth-led red-white Equipment and Aura deck that draws cards equal to the number of Auras and Equipment attached to Wyleth when he attacks. The commander provides the deck's draw engine. It is a focused voltron strategy sustained through combat.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Card draw on attack equal to attached Auras and Equipment; equipment and Aura synergy; Wyleth as draw engine; voltron combat strategy
precons.mainStrategy: Equip and enchant Wyleth to draw cards equal to the number of Auras and Equipment attached; build one enormous threat with card advantage fueling the strategy

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Equipment and Aura fans who want a Boros deck with built-in card draw that solves the color pair's traditional resource problem
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike voltron strategies or those who find commander-reliant decks frustrating when the commander is removed repeatedly
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Boros players who want White's protective equipment structure and Red's aggressive combat drive - Wyleth solves Boros's card draw problem by making the commander itself the draw engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White equips and protects while Red drives aggression - Wyleth converts every Aura and Equipment attached to him into a card draw trigger, making protection and power the same action
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how a commander ability can solve a fundamental color weakness - Wyleth's draw trigger makes Boros self-sustaining in a way that teaches players to evaluate commanders as problem-solvers
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches equipment and Aura fundamentals in a clean Boros context; Wyleth's card draw makes the strategy feel rewarding rather than resource-starved
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to sequence equipment deployment to maximize draw triggers and how to protect Wyleth as the deck's engine rather than just a threat
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining how a single commander ability can compensate for a color pair's weakness; good for Boros identity and equipment strategy

precons.deckDescription: An Obuun-led Naya landfall deck that distributes +1/+1 counters and animates a land into a creature each combat. Obuun's dual ability makes every land drop both a board development and a potential combat threat. A fresh take on landfall that rewards aggressive play rather than pure value accumulation.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Landfall triggers on land entry; land animation into creature at combat; +1/+1 counter distribution; extra land plays
precons.secondaryTheme: Land animation (Obuun makes a land into a creature)
precons.mainStrategy: Play lands to trigger landfall payoffs; Obuun puts +1/+1 counters on a creature and can animate a land into a creature each combat - winning through land-fueled board development

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Landfall fans who want a Naya take on the archetype with an animated land combat angle; players who enjoy creature-land hybrid strategies
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a lands-combo deck; this is a straightforward landfall aggro strategy without high combo ceiling
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Naya players who value Green's land mastery, Red's combat aggression, and White's structured creature buffs - Obuun combines all three into a land-animated combat strategy

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green grows and multiplies the land base, Red channels that land energy into animated combat threats, and White provides the counter distribution that makes each land drop a creature buff
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Naya uses landfall differently from typical Green-Blue builds - not just drawing cards but creating combat threats, teaching players that landfall payoffs can be creature-focused
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Accessible: play lands, trigger landfall, attack with animated land creatures. Obuun makes the payoff visible and immediate, teaching landfall as a combat engine
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to maximize landfall triggers through fetch lands, extra land plays, and bounce lands - and how Obuun's animated lands create surprise combat threats
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good Naya landfall example; useful for showing how landfall can be a combat strategy rather than purely a value or combo strategy

precons.deckDescription: An Anowon-led Dimir Rogue tribal deck that mills opponents when Rogues deal unblocked combat damage and draws cards for each Rogue that connects. Creates a dual threat: depleting opponent libraries while generating card advantage from those same hits.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Rogue tribal combat damage triggers; mill on unblocked Rogue damage; card draw from combat connection; evasion focus
precons.mainStrategy: Attack with unblocked Rogues to mill opponents; Anowon draws a card whenever a Rogue deals combat damage and mills; depletes opponent libraries while generating card advantage

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Rogue tribal fans and mill-adjacent players who want a clean two-color aggro deck with library attrition as a secondary win condition
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want dedicated mill; the mill here is a byproduct of combat damage rather than a primary strategy
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Dimir players who want Blue's evasive rogues and Black's attrition tools combined - Anowon rewards unblocked combat with both card draw and library depletion

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue provides the evasion that lets Rogues connect, while Black converts those connections into resource denial - every unblocked attack strips the opponent's library and refills yours
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Dimir approaches tribal differently - not just buffing creatures but building a two-pronged attack that depletes both opponent life total and library simultaneously
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches evasion as a strategic tool beyond just dealing damage - Anowon shows that unblocked creatures can generate card draw and mill, teaching players to value damage that connects
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build toward consistent Rogue damage connection through evasion, removal, and timing - and how mill scales as a win condition when opponents are low on cards
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Clean Dimir Rogue tribal example; good for explaining how Black and Blue combine evasion with resource denial in a tribal context

precons.deckDescription: A Jirina-led Mardu Human tribal deck that creates 1/1 Human tokens and buffs all Humans when Jirina enters. Sacrifice synergies add an aristocrats layer to the tribal core. Features partner commanders Trynn and Silvar as a strong alternate build for Human breeding and sacrifice loops.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Human tribal ETB token creation and anthem; Jirina enters-the-battlefield trigger; sacrifice synergies; Trynn and Silvar partner backup; aristocrats subtheme
precons.mainStrategy: Build an army of Humans pumped by Jirina's ETB counters; sacrifice them for aristocrats value to finish opponents off

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Human tribal fans who want a Mardu deck with aristocrats depth; players who enjoy combat-focused tribal with a sacrifice subtheme
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a pure aristocrats or pure tribal experience without overlap; the dual theme can feel unfocused without upgrades
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mardu players who combine White's Human community, Red's aggressive combat drive, and Black's willingness to sacrifice allies for power - Jirina leads a tribe that fights and dies productively

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White creates the Human army and imbues it with solidarity, Red drives it into aggressive combat, and Black extracts value when those Humans fall - a civilization that weaponizes its own casualties
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Shows how Mardu approaches Human tribal differently from Boros - adding Black's sacrifice dimension creates an aristocrats layer that rewards both attacking and dying
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Good introduction to how tribal and aristocrats synergies overlap - playing Jirina teaches players that creatures can generate value both while alive and when they die
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to balance attacking (to use Human buffs) with holding back for sacrifice fodder - managing the tension between aggression and value extraction
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Solid Mardu tribal example; useful for explaining how Black adds a sacrifice dimension to White's Human tribal identity

precons.deckDescription: A Kalamax-led Temur instants deck that copies the first instant cast each turn while Kalamax is tapped, and grows Kalamax with a +1/+1 counter whenever an instant is copied. Rewards reactive play patterns and holding up mana across opponents' turns for maximum copy triggers.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Kalamax instant copy when tapped; +1/+1 counter on Kalamax per copy; first instant per turn triggers; reactive play and instant-speed priority
precons.mainStrategy: Cast the first instant each turn while Kalamax is tapped to copy it; grow Kalamax with +1/+1 counters whenever instants are copied; maximize value from each instant cast

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Instant-focused players who want a Temur deck that copies spells and grows a commander through combat; players who enjoy reactive play patterns
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer sorcery-speed strategies or those who find holding up mana each turn mentally taxing
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Temur players who want Blue's instant precision, Red's explosive copy payoffs, and Green's mana base - Kalamax rewards playing at instant speed with both spell copies and a growing commander

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green builds the mana base to hold up instants, Blue selects the right instant at the right moment, and Red copies it for explosive value - Temur's reaction speed taken to its logical extreme
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches players to think at instant speed - holding up mana, evaluating board states on opponents' turns, and maximizing Kalamax's copy trigger through careful tapping management
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches instant-speed play and the value of holding up mana; Kalamax's tapped requirement trains players to plan their combat step strategically to enable spell copies
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to sequence attacks to keep Kalamax tapped during opponents' turns, maximizing copy triggers while also growing Kalamax with +1/+1 counters
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining instant-speed play patterns and how Temur approaches reactive spell-copying differently from Izzet

precons.deckDescription: A Kathril-led Abzan keyword ability counter deck that distributes keyword counters (flying, deathtouch, lifelink, etc.) to creatures based on keywords present in the graveyard. Intentionally fills the graveyard with keyword-dense creatures to maximize Kathril's entry impact.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Keyword ability counters from Ikoria; Kathril distributes graveyard keywords on ETB; graveyard keyword density as deckbuilding goal; flying, deathtouch, lifelink, hexproof counter distribution
precons.mainStrategy: Fill graveyard with creatures that have keyword abilities; cast Kathril to distribute keyword ability counters (flying, deathtouch, lifelink, etc.) equal to keywords among creatures in graveyard

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who want a creative combat deck built around keyword ability counters; graveyard enthusiasts who want a unique Abzan experience
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike tracking many different counter types; those who prefer straightforward creature combat without graveyard setup
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Abzan players who value White's keyword protection (lifelink, vigilance), Black's deathtouch and graveyard filling, and Green's creature base - Kathril harvests every dead creature's best ability

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White's protective keywords, Black's lethal abilities, and Green's physical prowess each contribute to Kathril's counter distribution - every dead creature leaves its best trait behind as a permanent gift
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Introduces keyword ability counters as a mechanic and teaches players how graveyard composition directly affects the board state Kathril creates - deckbuilding lesson in keyword density
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how keyword ability counters work and how deliberately filling the graveyard with keyword-rich creatures maximizes Kathril's impact on entry
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches graveyard deckbuilding with a specific goal: maximizing the variety and power of keywords available for Kathril to distribute - a targeted version of the classic reanimator setup
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining keyword ability counters and how Abzan approaches graveyard strategies through creature keywords rather than raw recursion

precons.deckDescription: A Gavi-led Jeskai cycling deck that allows the first cycling activation each turn to be free, triggering payoffs for each cycled card. Multiple win conditions (Brallin/Shabraz, Zenith Flare, The Locust God) give the deck several ways to convert cycling into a finish.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Gavi free cycling once per turn; cycling payoff triggers; Brallin and Shabraz as partner alternate commanders; Zenith Flare as win condition; The Locust God as token engine
precons.secondaryTheme: Cycling payoffs / free cycle each turn
precons.mainStrategy: Cycle cards freely each turn via Gavi's ability; trigger cycling payoffs to generate tokens and draw; finish with Zenith Flare, The Locust God, or Brallin/Shabraz

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White generates the community (tokens) and protects them with order, while Green ensures the community grows and becomes powerful - Selesnya's philosophy of collective strength made mechanical

learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Ideal first Commander deck for players who want to make lots of creatures and attack with everything - Selesnya token go-wide is intuitive, satisfying, and teaches both color identities clearly

learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful beginner Selesnya example for learning White-Green token strategies

precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Urza Construct token scaling with artifact count; artifact menace anthem; artifact creature go-wide; retro frame aesthetic throughout
precons.secondaryTheme: Artifact synergies / payoffs for artifact count
precons.mainStrategy: Fill the board with artifact creatures; Urza creates a Construct token and gives your artifact creatures menace; retro card frame aesthetic throughout

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Artifact players who want a Esper go-wide artifact strategy; fans of The Brothers' War lore who want Urza's perspective; players who appreciate the retro card frame aesthetic
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer artifact combo over artifact go-wide; Urza's deck wants a battlefield of creatures rather than a few powerful artifacts
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Esper players who combine White's ordered artifact armies, Blue's artifact engineering precision, and Black's willingness to arm any tool for dominance - Urza's Iron Alliance is a disciplined machine army

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White organizes the artifact army in formation, Blue designs each construct with purpose, and Black weaponizes even the most mundane artifact - Esper's three colors each contributing a different dimension of artifice
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches go-wide artifact strategy and how Urza's menace anthem converts artifact quantity into combat inevitability - a lesson in how board presence scales with artifact count
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how artifact creature tribal synergies work and how Urza's Construct token and menace ability create an army that's difficult to block profitably
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build a critical mass of artifact creatures and how Urza's Construct token scales with artifact count - a lesson in why artifact density creates exponential rather than linear board advantage
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of Esper go-wide artifacts; useful for showing how White-Blue-Black approaches artifacts through army scale rather than individual combo pieces

precons.deckDescription: A Mishra-led Grixis non-creature artifact deck that creates a copy of a non-creature artifact as an attacking 4/4 artifact creature each combat, sacrificed at end of turn. Ashnod the Uncaring creates escalating copy triggers from each sacrifice. A recursive animate-and-sacrifice artifact value loop.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Mishra non-creature artifact animation as 4/4 attacker; end-of-turn sacrifice; Ashnod copy trigger on sacrifice; artifact sacrifice value loop
precons.mainStrategy: Transform non-creature artifacts into combat creatures with Mishra's ability; sacrifice them at end of turn; Ashnod (backup) generates extra value from those sacrifices

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Artifact players who want a sacrifice-value engine rather than go-wide; those who enjoy Ashnod's sacrifice payoffs as a secondary commander
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a typical artifact-creature strategy; Mishra's deck specifically uses non-creature artifacts as its primary resource
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Grixis players who combine Blue's artifact engineering, Black's sacrifice ambition, and Red's destructive consumption - Mishra transforms artifacts into killing machines, uses them, then discards them for Ashnod's value

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue designs the artifact, Red animates it into a weapon, and Black harvests its death - Mishra's philosophy that artifacts are tools to be used and discarded perfectly captures Grixis's resource-exploitation identity
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches how non-creature artifacts can be animated and sacrificed as a value loop and how Ashnod the Uncaring creates escalating copy effects from each sacrifice
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches the animate-then-sacrifice artifact loop and how Mishra's ability creates temporary but powerful artifact creatures from your non-creature artifacts each combat
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to identify which non-creature artifacts create the best Mishra animations and how Ashnod's copy trigger scales with sacrifice frequency for exponential value
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining non-creature artifact animation and how Grixis approaches artifacts through sacrifice loops rather than go-wide strategies

precons.deckDescription: An Abaddon-led Grixis Cascade deck that gives all spells cascade when opponents have lost life this turn. Enables Cascade chains off any spell on damage turns, creating explosive multi-spell turns. Be'lakor provides a strong Demon tribal alternate commander.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Abaddon Cascade trigger on life-loss turns; global Cascade for all spells; Cascade chain potential; Be'lakor Demon tribal backup commander
precons.mainStrategy: Abaddon gives spells cascade when opponents have lost life this turn; chain cascades for free spells; Be'lakor enables Demon tribal as an alternate commander path

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Cascade fans and Demon tribal players who want two powerful strategies in one deck; Warhammer fans who want the Chaos faction
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who dislike random free spells; Cascade's inherent randomness makes this deck inconsistent if the Cascade chain doesn't cooperate
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Grixis players who want Blue's cunning, Black's demonic power, and Red's chaotic cascade energy - Abaddon turns opponents' life loss into a global Cascade trigger, making each combat a chain reaction

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black summons the demons, Red triggers the chaotic cascade, and Blue ensures the chain reaches its most valuable payoffs - the Ruinous Powers deck embodies Grixis's philosophy of using chaos as a weapon
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches Cascade as a triggered mechanic and how Abaddon's life-loss condition enables it every combat - a lesson in how conditional abilities can make powerful mechanics accessible consistently
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Cascade mechanics and how building a deck with a spread of CMC values maximizes Cascade value - an accessible lesson in how free spell mechanics reward careful deck construction
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build a Cascade deck by managing CMC distribution and how Be'lakor's Demon tribal path offers an alternative win condition if Cascade chains underperform
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining Cascade and how a life-loss trigger can make the mechanic consistently accessible in Grixis

precons.deckDescription: A Swarmlord-led Temur Tyranid tribal deck with the Ravenous mechanic, which rewards investing five or more mana into X-cost creatures with additional ETB payoffs. The Swarmlord distributes +1/+1 counters to Tyranids when a creature enters, while Magus Lucea Kane offers an alternate X-spell plan.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Ravenous mechanic rewarding 5+ mana X-cost investment; Tyranid tribal +1/+1 counter distribution; Swarmlord ETB triggers; Magus Lucea Kane as preferred alternate commander
precons.mainStrategy: Invest mana in X-cost spells with Ravenous; The Swarmlord gives Tyranids +1/+1 counters as creatures enter; Magus Lucea Kane provides an alternate X-spell commander plan

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Counter and X-spell players interested in the Ravenous mechanic and variable mana investment
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a straightforward creature deck; X-cost management and counter tracking require significant attention
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Temur players who want Green's mana generation, Blue's counter precision, and Red's explosive X-cost payoffs - The Swarmlord converts every creature ETB into a +1/+1 counter, making mana investment directly proportional to board state

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green generates the mana for massive X-costs, Blue tracks and multiplies the counters with precision, and Red channels the resulting power into devastating attacks - Temur's growth philosophy taken to its biological extreme
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches the Ravenous mechanic (X-cost reward at 5+) and how investing large amounts into X-cost spells scales both the creature and the Ravenous bonus simultaneously
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches X-cost mechanics and how Ravenous creates an incentive to invest the maximum possible mana - a lesson in how scaling mechanics reward mana commitment
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build an X-cost deck by maximizing mana generation (Green ramp) and identifying which X-cost spells provide the best Ravenous payoffs at 5+ investment
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example for explaining X-cost mechanics, Ravenous, and a counter-focused Commander plan

precons.deckDescription: An Inquisitor Greyfax-led Esper token deck featuring the Squad mechanic, which lets you pay a cost multiple times to create multiple tokens. Marneus Calgar offers an alternate commander whose triggered ability draws cards as tokens enter.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Squad mechanic for multiple token creation; Marneus Calgar card draw on every creature ETB; token quantity payoffs; Esper go-wide with draw engine
precons.mainStrategy: Use Squad to multiply creature tokens entering the battlefield; Marneus Calgar offers an alternate command plan that turns token creation into card draw

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Token players interested in the Squad mechanic as a repeatable token multiplier
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer non-token strategies; the deck is aggressively optimized for token generation and may feel overwhelming in casual pods
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Esper players who want White's token formation, Blue's precise card draw from tokens, and Black's threatening presence - Marneus Calgar as backup commander draws from every token created, making the deck generate card advantage at an alarming rate

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White creates the troops in formation, Blue draws a card for each one entering the battlefield, and Black ensures every token has threatening presence - the Imperium's army is both vast and intelligent
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches Squad as a repeatable additional-cost mechanic and shows how Marneus Calgar can turn token creation into card draw
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Squad mechanics and how Marneus Calgar converts token generation into card draw - an accessible lesson in how token commanders that draw cards create self-sustaining engines
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to maximize Marneus Calgar's card draw trigger by building around token generation across multiple permanent types (creatures, treasures, clues, food) for maximum triggers per turn
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful example of a token deck with a built-in card-draw engine and for explaining Squad

precons.deckDescription: A Szarekh-led mono-Black artifact deck featuring Biotransference, which makes all creatures artifacts in all zones. Multiple strong commanders (Imotekh, Anrakyr, Trazyn, Illuminor Szeras) provide flexible build directions within a self-mill and artifact recursion strategy.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Biotransference converting all creatures to artifacts; mono-Black artifact identity via graveyard; self-mill artifact strategy; multiple strong backup commanders
precons.mainStrategy: Fill graveyard via self-mill; use artifacts and artifact-creature synergies; Biotransference turns all creatures into artifacts in all zones; multiple strong commander options beyond Szarekh

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Mono-Black artifact fans who want a fresh take on the archetype with multiple strong commander options; Warhammer 40k fans who want the Necron faction
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a focused mono-Black experience without artifact complexity; the artifact focus is unusual for Black and requires embracing a different Black identity
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mono-Black players who want to explore Black's relationship with artifacts as a non-Green technology - Necron Dynasties teaches that Black can build artifact-based power through self-mill and recursion rather than construction

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Black's dominion over death extends to machines in Necron form - these ancient robots don't construct artifacts, they reclaim them from the grave, giving Black an artifact identity rooted in recursion rather than creation
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates that mono-Black can build a powerful artifact strategy through graveyard recursion rather than traditional artifact construction, teaching players that Black's relationship with artifacts is unique
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches how Biotransference creates a unified artifact theme by converting all creatures into artifacts, making every graveyard interaction also an artifact interaction
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to evaluate the multiple commander options (Szarekh, Imotekh, Anrakyr, Trazyn, Illuminor Szeras) and choose the one that best fits your preferred play style within the same 99
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining mono-Black artifacts as a distinct identity from artifact-focused multicolor decks; good for teaching Biotransference's unique rules implications

precons.deckDescription: A Jared Carthalion-led five-color Domain and WUBRG deck that rewards casting spells with all five colors in their casting costs. Jared generates +1/+1 counters from combat damage and produces mana of all five colors, making him both a resource generator and a combat threat.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Domain mechanic scaling with basic land types; WUBRG casting cost payoffs; Jared mana generation and counter growth; five-color chromatic identity
precons.mainStrategy: Play cards with all five colors in their costs for maximum Domain and WUBRG payoffs; Jared Carthalion generates +1/+1 counters and mana when opponents deal combat damage to him

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Five-color players who want a focused identity beyond goodstuff; players who enjoy the challenge of building around high-pip casting costs
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a consistent, linear game plan; Domain and WUBRG strategies require a diverse mana base that can be unreliable in early turns
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Five-color players who want to embody all five philosophies equally - Jared Carthalion rewards casting the most colorful spells, making the identity itself the engine

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: All five colors working together toward maximum chromatic expression - Domain rewards having all basic land types and WUBRG costs reward a fully diverse mana base, making the five-color identity mechanically synergistic
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches Domain and WUBRG mechanics and how building around color diversity creates a focused identity even in five-color - the theme IS the color identity itself
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Domain as a scaling mechanic and how WUBRG casting costs reward diverse mana bases - a lesson in how five-color can be a focused strategy rather than just 'everything good'
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches mana base construction for five-color decks and how to balance domain enablers (basic land types) with powerful WUBRG payoff cards
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of a focused five-color identity; useful for explaining how Domain and WUBRG mechanics reward building with all five colors intentionally

precons.deckDescription: A Dihada-led Mardu legendary-matters deck where every permanent is legendary and Dihada rewards casting legendary spells with one of four different payoffs. The most thematically committed precon Wizards has made, with near-universal legendary creature density.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Legendary permanents matter; Dihada four-mode legendary reward triggers; near-universal legendary density; variable reward based on legendary type cast
precons.secondaryTheme: Variable rewards from Dihada for legendary spells
precons.mainStrategy: Every creature and most permanents are legendary; Dihada provides different rewards (draw, vigilance, lifelink, etc.) for casting legendary spells; one of the most thematically committed precons

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy legendary-matters strategies and want the most thematically committed precon Wizards has made; Dominaria lore fans
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want flexibility in card selection; the all-legendary constraint limits the card pool significantly
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Mardu players who want White's heroic order, Red's legendary warrior spirit, and Black's commanding ambition - Dihada rewards every legendary spell with a variable bonus, making each legendary feel like a story beat

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White honors legendary history, Red celebrates legendary warriors, and Black collects legendary power - Dihada binds their wills and distributes rewards for each legend that joins her cause
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates the legendary-matters theme at its most committed and teaches players how building around a card type rather than a mechanic creates a distinctive and cohesive deck identity
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches legendary-matters as a deckbuilding constraint and how Dihada's variable rewards create different payoffs for different game states - a lesson in reading what reward is needed when
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to evaluate legendary creatures for both their individual power and their ability to trigger Dihada's best rewards, creating a two-dimensional card evaluation framework
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful legendary-matters example showing how Mardu's colors contribute different relationships with legendary permanents

precons.deckDescription: A Nalia-led Orzhov Party deck that gives party members deathtouch and lets you draw when a party member deals combat damage. It asks the player to maintain a Wizard, Rogue, Cleric, and Warrior simultaneously for full Party payoffs.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Party mechanic requiring four creature classes; Nalia deathtouch grant and card draw on party damage; multi-type tribal across Wizard, Rogue, Cleric, Warrior
precons.mainStrategy: Control one of each party class (Wizard, Rogue, Cleric, Warrior) to unlock maximum Party payoffs; Nalia gives party members deathtouch and lets you draw when a party member deals damage

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy multi-type tribal strategies, the Party mechanic, and its D&D thematic fit
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a single-tribe tribal experience; managing four creature types simultaneously requires deck-building awareness that can feel constraining
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Orzhov players who combine White's structured party composition (every role filled) with Black's dark utility (deathtouch assassins, cunning rogues) - the party is disciplined and deadly

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: White enforces the party's structure and fills each role with purpose, while Black arms the party with lethal tools - together they create the most dangerous adventuring party in the dungeon
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches the Party mechanic and how maintaining four creature types creates a multi-tribal strategy that's more complex than single-tribe decks
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Party as a multi-type tribal mechanic and how to build a deck that covers all four classes; accessible because the creature types (Wizard, Rogue, Cleric, Warrior) span many existing tribal archetypes
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build for Party completion efficiently - identifying creatures that fill multiple roles or enable quick party assembly is the key deckbuilding skill this deck develops
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Useful Party-mechanic example for explaining how multi-class tribal works in a D&D-themed Commander strategy

precons.deckDescription: A Captain N'ghathrod-led Dimir Horror tribal deck that mills opponents when Horrors deal combat damage and allows stealing of milled creatures. A mill-theft hybrid strategy where the same combat damage that fills opponents' graveyards provides a creature acquisition engine.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Horror tribal mill on combat damage; creature theft from milled opponent libraries; Captain N'ghathrod combat triggers; mill-theft combination
precons.mainStrategy: Build a Horror board; Captain N'ghathrod mills opponents when Horrors deal combat damage and lets you steal milled creatures; mill as both disruption and creature acquisition

recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players in groups with heavy graveyard hate; those who dislike mill strategies or find stealing opponents' cards unsatisfying due to variance
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Dimir players who want Blue's library invasion and Black's creature theft combined - Captain N'ghathrod turns each Horror's combat damage into both mill and a chance to steal the milled creatures

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue strips opponents' knowledge and resources through mill, while Black claims the best of what's taken - every Horror that connects is both an information advantage and a potential creature acquisition
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Dimir can build a tribal strategy around an unusual tribe (Horrors) with a non-combat win condition (mill-theft), showing the breadth of how tribal mechanics can be structured
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches mill-theft as a connected strategy - the same combat damage that fills opponents' graveyards gives you the option to take their best creatures, making each attack a two-pronged threat
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to maximize Horror combat connections through evasion and removal, and how to evaluate which milled creatures are worth stealing vs leaving in the graveyard
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Strong example for explaining mill-theft strategies and Horror tribal; useful for showing how Dimir can use mill as a creature acquisition engine rather than just a win condition

precons.deckDescription: A Firkraag-led Izzet Goad deck where Firkraag draws a card whenever a goaded creature deals combat damage. Primarily a Goad deck with Dragon flavor rather than dedicated Dragon tribal. Baeloth Barrityl is an equally popular alternative commander for pure Goad builds.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Goad mechanic as primary strategy; Firkraag card draw from goaded creature damage; Dragon flavor with limited tribal synergy; Baeloth alternate Goad commander
precons.mainStrategy: Goad opponents' creatures to force them to attack others; Firkraag draws cards when goaded creatures deal combat damage; first Dragon-Goad hybrid deck - feels more like a Goad deck than tribal

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Goad enthusiasts who also enjoy Dragon flavor; players who want an Izzet deck that creates political chaos rather than pure spellslinging
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players expecting a typical Dragon tribal experience; the deck feels more like a Goad deck with Dragons as flavor than a dedicated tribal build
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Izzet players who want Blue's political manipulation combined with Red's draconic aggression - Firkraag draws cards whenever goaded creatures deal combat damage, making opponents' fights profitable for you

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue engineers the political situation with precision (who is goaded, who attacks whom), while Red watches with gleeful satisfaction as the goaded Dragons tear each other apart - Izzet as a chaos architect
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how Goad can be built into a Dragon-flavored deck, teaching players that tribal and political mechanics can coexist when the commander rewards the political action (card draw from goaded damage)
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Goad as a forced-attack political mechanic and how drawing cards from goaded creature damage creates passive card advantage - an accessible lesson in political value generation
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to maximize Firkraag's card draw by goading creatures with high power values and how to protect yourself from the combat chaos you create
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of Goad in an Izzet context; useful for showing how political mechanics can generate card advantage rather than just table chaos

precons.deckDescription: A Faldorn-led Gruul exile-casting deck that creates a Wolf token whenever a spell is cast from exile. Combines Cascade, Adventure, impulse draw, and Madness as multiple exile-cast enablers under a single token-generation payoff.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Wolf token on exile cast via Faldorn; Cascade as exile-cast enabler; Adventure, impulse draw, Madness as additional exile sources; token generation from spell variety
precons.mainStrategy: Cast spells from exile via Cascade, Adventures, Madness, impulse draw and other exile-cast effects; Faldorn creates a Wolf token each time a spell is cast from exile

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Exile-casting fans who want a Gruul deck that rewards Cascade, Adventures, and impulse draw with Wolf token generation
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a focused game plan; the exile-casting theme spans many different mechanics that can make the deck feel scattered
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Gruul players who want Red's impulsive exile casting and Green's creature-token payoffs combined - Faldorn makes every spell cast from exile produce a Wolf, turning variety into volume

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Red casts impulsively from whatever exile zone is available, Green converts each cast into a creature token, and Faldorn unifies the chaos into a consistent Wolf-producing engine
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Demonstrates how multiple exile-casting mechanics (Cascade, Adventure, impulse draw, Madness) can be unified under one payoff trigger, teaching players to recognize a family of related mechanics
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches exile casting as a category of mechanics and how Faldorn's Wolf trigger converts all of them into consistent token generation regardless of which specific mechanic produced the cast
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to identify and stack exile-casting enablers across different mechanics and how Wolf token accumulation scales with the number of different exile-cast sources in the deck
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining exile casting as a unified mechanic family; excellent for showing how Gruul can build a token engine from spell-casting rather than creature play

precons.deckDescription: A Kamiz-led Esper Connive deck that makes the highest-power attacker unblockable and causes it to Connive when it deals combat damage. A distinctly aggressive Esper deck that uses evasion and card selection through combat rather than traditional control tools.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Connive via Kamiz unblockable trigger; highest-power attacker unblockable; looting on combat damage; +1/+1 counter generation from Connive
precons.mainStrategy: Attack with cheap evasive creatures; Connive lets attackers loot and place +1/+1 counters; Kamiz makes the highest-power attacker unblockable and connives it; backup commander supports voting

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who want an Esper deck focused on attacking rather than controlling; those who enjoy Connive for its looting and counter-stacking rewards
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players expecting a traditional Esper control deck; the evasive attacker focus is a significant departure from typical White-Blue-Black gameplay
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Esper players who want Blue's evasion and card selection, White's protective order, and Black's cunning manipulation - Kamiz makes the largest attacker unblockable each combat, rewarding building toward one dominant threat

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Esper typically controls from a distance, but here it strikes precisely - White protects the attack, Blue ensures it connects unblocked, and Black's Connive loot converts each hit into card selection
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Subverts Esper's typical control identity by showing the color combination can support an aggressive evasive attacker strategy, teaching players that color identity is flexible
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Connive as a combat reward mechanic - connecting with attackers isn't just damage, it's card selection and creature growth, making every attack meaningful
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to sequence attackers by power value to maximize Kamiz's unblockable trigger and how Connive's loot effect helps find key pieces mid-combat
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example of Esper defying its control reputation; useful for explaining Connive and how New Capenna's crime families gave familiar color combinations new identities

precons.deckDescription: An Anhelo-led Grixis Casualty deck where Anhelo has Casualty 2 - sacrifice a creature with power 2 or more to copy any instant or sorcery. The most combo-potential of the New Capenna precons, held back by insufficient token generators for consistent Casualty payment.
precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Anhelo Casualty 2 for spell copying; sacrifice creature to copy instant or sorcery; spellslinger with sacrifice cost; token generators needed for consistency
precons.mainStrategy: Sacrifice a creature (Casualty) to copy an instant or sorcery; Anhelo has Casualty 2 - sacrifice a 2-power creature to copy any instant/sorcery cast; noted as underperforming due to sacrifice cost but strong spellslinger skeleton

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Spellslinger players who want a Grixis shell with spell-copying potential; those willing to upgrade the sacrifice enablers to unlock the deck's true power
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who want a ready-to-play experience; the Casualty mechanic underperforms out of the box due to insufficient token generators
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Grixis players who want Blue's precise spell selection, Black's willingness to sacrifice creatures as spell fuel, and Red's explosive copy payoffs - the deck's potential matches Grixis's high-ceiling identity

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Blue selects the spell worth copying, Black provides the sacrifice cost willingly, and Red copies it explosively - Casualty embodies Grixis's philosophy that nothing is too precious to sacrifice for the right moment
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches Casualty as a mechanic and the core spellslinger-sacrifice tension - when is copying a spell worth the creature cost? A nuanced lesson in value assessment
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Casualty's sacrifice-to-copy mechanic and how token generators solve the creature-cost problem - an accessible lesson in how to fix a mechanic's built-in limitation
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to build around Casualty by including token generators that make the sacrifice cost negligible while still enabling powerful spell copies
learningProfile.voxManaBasicsPageUse: Good example for explaining Casualty and how a mechanic's effectiveness depends on supporting cards; honest case study in a deck that requires upgrades

precons.notesMechanicsMentioned: Blitz alternate casting cost for haste and draw; Henzie cost reduction scaling with attacks; ETB value from temporary haste creatures; big creature deployment
precons.mainStrategy: Cast creatures with Blitz (pay alternate cost, give haste, sacrifice at end of turn, draw a card); Henzie reduces Blitz costs by 1 for each time he's attacked; cheat out high-CMC creatures for their ETB effects

recommendationProfile.recommendedFor: Players who enjoy high-CMC creature strategies with haste and ETB value; those who want a Jund deck with a distinct identity beyond typical aggro
recommendationProfile.notRecommendedFor: Players who prefer steady board development; Blitz is inherently temporary and can feel inconsistent if the draw-a-card compensation doesn't chain into more action
recommendationProfile.voxManaPlacementFit: Jund players who value Black's willingness to sacrifice, Red's haste-fueled aggression, and Green's enormous creature pool - Henzie scales Blitz costs down with each attack, rewarding consistent pressure

learningProfile.colorPhilosophySummary: Green's enormous creatures become Red's temporary weapons and Black's sacrificial tools - Blitz is Jund's philosophy of burning everything for maximum immediate impact, consequences be damned
learningProfile.whatThisDeckTeachesAboutItsColors: Teaches Blitz as a haste-ETB-sacrifice loop and how Henzie's attack-scaling creates a feedback loop where aggression directly reduces future creature costs
learningProfile.beginnerLesson: Teaches Blitz as an alternate cost mechanic and how ETB effects combined with haste create immediate value that compensates for the creature's temporary nature
learningProfile.strategyLesson: Teaches how to evaluate which creatures are worth Blitzing vs casting normally, and how Henzie's cost reduction scales through the game to enable increasingly explosive turns
